precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” is not talking about all people. The man is Adam, and verse 28 shows it: God blessed them and told them to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” That is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

Genesis 2:7 is read together with it: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Formed from the dust of the ground: we know God is black, Christ is black and the apostles were black. The real Jews are black, and the Caucasian race, Esau as the Bible calls them, is cursed.

Solomon says the same in Wisdom of Solomon 7, that he is “the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, and that God gave him to know “the operation of the elements.” The elements in the soil are the elements in man: oxygen, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, in different percentages. When God made us from the dust, he took from those elements and worked them to form man, the way he formed land and sea. That is what we call the periodic table today, and it is what Esau tries to do with his so-called science: play Frankenstein and try to become God.

But the image goes deeper than the dust and the skin. The breath God breathed in is wisdom, “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” He gave it to us so that we would know better. Being made after his image and likeness is his spirit, the commandments of God.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:24
precepts.why:
After his image and after his likeness means his spirit, the commandments of God. A lot of the time people think the image and likeness only means looking like God. Ephesians 4:24 shows what his image is: “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

That is after the image of God: created in righteousness. The man God made in his image was made to be righteous and holy, not only to share his color.

So being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; you are still the devil. We say the white man is a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black does not make you special unless you are righteous. It is the laws of God that make us special.

precepts.label: Psalms 17:15
precepts.why:
Genesis says “after our likeness”, and Psalms 17:15 shows what that likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is righteousness. David beholds God's face in righteousness and is satisfied to wake in his likeness. So man made after God's image and likeness was meant to be righteous.

Read with Ephesians 4:24, the new man “created in righteousness and true holiness”, it is plain: black is black, but being made in his image means being black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. We say the white man's a devil, but there's black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous; it is the laws of God that make us special. The dust of the ground made the body; keeping the commandments is what makes us his likeness.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:10
precepts.why:
Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:5-8
precepts.why:
At the golden calf “the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.” What was that rose up to play? You think it was hopscotch? Paul explains it.

“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” He is quoting the very verse, and before it he says: “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” When they lusted after evil things, that is the rose up to play.

The verse before that: “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” Why were they overthrown in the wilderness? Because they lusted after evil things.

Then verse 8: “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” So we understand the rose up to play was fornication. They lusted after evil things, and it destroyed us.

The nations understood this. When we are in sin, they know what will happen, they can destroy us. So when they took their crafty counsel they said, how do we keep these people in error? They like to rap, so give them murder music and lascivious music. That is why they give our sisters these songs, so vulgar. Their whole plan is to keep us in sin. Pleasure now, regret later: you are going to pay.

precepts.label: Luke 1:68-74
precepts.why:
Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

precepts.label: Numbers 25:18
precepts.why:
“the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” “And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.” What would cause us to bow down to their gods? It just says they committed whoredom. It was sex that got the people to worship another god, and “Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.”

Jump to the end of the chapter: “For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor”. They vex you with their wiles, their seduction, and beguiled you into worshipping their gods. They knew: we have to get these people to sin against their God. So they used this tricknology, this stratagem, to move them away from God. That was the popular plan. “and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, which was slain in the day of the plague for Peor’s sake.”

“For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world”. It was Moab then, and it is all the nations now. Today the majority of the pornography is controlled by Amalek and Edom. They understood: we are going to destroy the minds of the people. We are not the only race having sex, but all our music is derogatory and evil, every video is a twerk video, and even somebody’s grandmother is twerking online. Everything is over-sexualized to destroy the minds of our young people, along with the drugs, the whoring and the music.

These are the wiles of the devil. The Lord would not let Balaam curse Israel, so the counsel was to make Israel fall through whoredom. As long as we continue in whoredom we will not build healthy marriages, we will not produce spiritually healthy children, and the generational curses keep going. Our strength is to come back to the laws of God.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 7:6-10
thread.text: For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Leviticus 20:26
precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself”. He chose you to be special unto him, set apart from everybody else. So the question is: what makes us holy? What scripture?

Leviticus 20:26 was brought from the floor as the answer: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” The Lord is holy, and he severed Israel from other people to be his. That severing is the same set-apart people of Deuteronomy 7:6, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

So there has to be something we are doing that makes us different. We cannot be doing the same thing the world is doing, and we cannot be doing what the churches are doing. What severs us from the other people is the laws of God being applied, which is what Romans 7:12 goes on to show.

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
“Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” If the law is holy, and God says you are a holy people, then we are supposed to be a law-abiding people. The laws of God are our constitution, the thing we stand on. That is what makes us holy, what makes us special, what makes us set apart: the laws being applied.

The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says to do. Other than that it is just pages, just words on a page, just a book. The word is alive and living when you let it live through you by your actions. You become the word, the living example of what it means to be a holy people. That is why the nations say, what a wise and understanding people. They see our actions.

We witness that already at the big events in the big arenas. They say, thousands of black men and nobody smoking weed, no fights breaking out. Then look at what happened in Houston at the rodeo, and how they laughed at us; we are a joke to them. But when we move they ask, how are they so organized, how can they mobilize a few thousand men, put them on the street and file them back in like that, nobody fighting and the place clean? That is the word of God working through us. There is a standard we live by because we are gods on the earth, and it is second nature to us as a nation.

So do not walk in hypocrisy. God gave us something that will make us shine bright and obtain the kingdom. Be that living example to the people.

precepts.label: Matthew 9:36
precepts.why:
“But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.” As Christ went out teaching, healing and doing miracles, he looked and saw that his people fainted. They were out in the streets, they did not worship their God, and their own leaders were taking advantage of them at that time.

It is the same in this captivity as in the time of Rome. Look at our people out there: they are lost, they have no shepherd, they are confused. Not only have the people of the world taken advantage of us, but our own people take advantage too, using the knowledge to get preeminence.

So leaders are motivated because we see the same thing Christ saw: our people afflicted, with no leaders, and looking for a shepherd, which is Christ ultimately. Instead of benefiting ourselves, we see the decayed state of our people and make the sacrifices. To hell with the riches, to hell with the women, having sex, and all those other things. We do whatever it takes to rebuild our nation, so that we can truly benefit from each other and have one shepherd rule over us, with nobody able to take advantage of us.

That is the mind the Lord has put in us, and those who carry it are the ones standing in these last days, speaking with authority and showing our people: this is not the way; let us move according to this holy word and restore this nation. That is what it means to be the holy people God chose.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:19
precepts.why:
“There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” You cannot be a hypocrite, especially in a leadership position. Look at the other camps: they are supposed to be leading the people, but their mind is on the riches, or on how many bodies they can put as a notch in their belt.

There is one that is supposed to be wise. What makes you wise? Keeping the commandments. Those leaders know that. They know they are Israel, they know they are God's chosen people, and they know they are supposed to be keeping the laws. Yet because of their bad intentions and covetousness, because their god is money, or their god is power to move and persuade the people, they are unprofitable to themselves.

And nothing will be hid. Everything that is done will be revealed in time. That is the other side of Deuteronomy 7: the Lord “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations; And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”. If you use a position to lead and teach the people and then take advantage of them, beguiling the sisters into sex, keeping them in a filthy mindset, or taking their money, God will judge you. You hate God and you hate his people.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 22:9
thread.text: Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: Sirach 26:19-21
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.” Reading that, we might think only of agriculture or farming, but it is talking about much more than that, and Sirach 26 shows what.

“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” The strangers are the heathen, the other nations. Then it explains how you give your strength to them: “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed.” A fruitful possession means you have a position, you have money, you are rich. Sow it with your own seed means sow it with your own people. You got money? Don't be going and marrying no damn white woman. What a lot of brothers do today, the first thing when they get money, is go marry a heathen. When you marry the heathen when you are rich, you are giving your strength unto strangers.

Instead, deal with your own people: start a family with the woman God created for you, “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Your stock is your nationality, your race, your people. You are a son of God; why would you want to go deal with other nations?

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” When you marry your sisters and bring forth children among your people, your children and your race are magnified. Good descent means your children are not confused about what their nationality is, because you did not sow your seed among all different kinds of heathen women, as our forefathers did in the book of Nehemiah.

That is the law of Deuteronomy 22:9. When we go and deal with other nations, the fruit of the vineyard is defiled: the children brought forth, the descendants, are defiled and confused.

thread.label: Deuteronomy 31:11-13
thread.text: When all Israel is come to appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose, thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.

classes.title: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 15:33
precepts.why:
Moses commanded: “thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.” In their hearing. “Gather the people together, men, and women, and children, and thy stranger that is within thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear the Lord your God, and observe to do all the words of this law”. Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God: in hearing we process what we heard, learn from it, and apply it to our life.

So we have to exercise these senses: in what we watch, as Job 31 was pulled up, and in our hearing, what we ingest and listen to. “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” What you digest in your vision and your hearing will change the way you think.

That is why the law is read in the hearing of the whole house, even “their children, which have not known any thing”, so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord. If the ear is filled with the law, it forms the mind in the law; if it is filled with evil communications, it corrupts the manners.

We exercise the physical senses, what we see and what we hear, so we can tap into the spiritual senses we have. Going from milk to meat means training the ear on the word of God and guarding it from everything that would corrupt it.

precepts.label: Matthew 18:20
precepts.why:
Elisha prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and the young man saw “the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” The Lord showed him something nobody could see: he opened his eyes, and he could see what was behind him. In the spiritual realm, there are angels all around us.

The Lord said it: “where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident, the way he opened the young man's eyes.

There will come a time when some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears, show us, direct our path and reveal things to us. That is one of the spiritual senses being activated, and part of it is having foresight.

But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. If you are still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. The Lord is in the midst of his people when they gather in his name; it is the ones who have come out of their sins whose eyes he opens to see it.

thread.label: 2 Chronicles 7:14-20
thread.text: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 4:13
precepts.why:
Who was the Lord talking to in 2 Chronicles 7? Solomon. “if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”, and “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes”, then “will I pluck them up by the roots”. So what was Solomon's problem, outside of the sin itself? Solomon tells it on himself: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.”

That was his problem. He couldn't take correction. He didn't want to hear it; nobody could tell him nothing. That's like some brothers here: they can't be told, they don't want to hear it, they get offended. He was an old, foolish king who could no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all the other problems he had.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that. All wisdom was given to him, and he saw his father's life before his eyes. He was concerned with how the world operated and wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from this world.

So the forsaking that brought the captivity began with a king who could not be admonished. When you keep repeating something to people who can't be told anything, after a while you lose them. That is why we have to be willing to receive correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 15:10
precepts.why:
The Lord warned Solomon, “if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments”; to forsake means to abandon, desert or leave something entirely, a breach of duty, to totally turn your back. Proverbs ties forsaking to hating correction: “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.”

When you have forsaken the way, being corrected is grievous to you. You keep having to be told the same thing over and over, and the one who doesn't want to hear it gets pissed off; he doesn't want to hear it no more. That was Solomon, the old and foolish king who would no more be admonished.

And the end of it is death: “he that hateth reproof shall die.” For Israel it meant being plucked up by the roots out of the land and made a proverb and a byword among all nations. Reading that is understanding why we are in captivity today. We got jammed up because we would not take correction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time the correction comes, he will not accept it. So he gets corrected over and over, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiffnecked. The scriptures don't have that effect on him anymore; there is no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers always getting stood up, and after a while it's, yeah, okay, put me out, I'll be back.

Why does that happen? The word of God is not moving you to change. You can't be the same person you were before; there has to be some type of growth. How do you find yourself doing the same thing you were doing ten years ago? Why, ten years later, does somebody have to motivate you to go do the work? Something is not firing off; something is disconnected.

The word of God is supposed to inspire you to change. The word of God changes you; the word of God can cure you. If you ain't changing, it is one of two things: you are a heathen, or you are a reprobate, and the kingdom ain't for you. So if it is not working, examine whether you even believe.

That is the other side of 2 Chronicles 7:14. The Lord will hear and forgive and heal the land when his people humble themselves and turn from their wicked ways. The one who hardens his neck against reproof is suddenly destroyed, and that without remedy.

precepts.label: Job 36:15
precepts.why:
Job 36:10 says the Lord “openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity”: he commanded, requested and called you to return from iniquity back to your heritage. Verse 15 shows where he opens those ears: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The poor here are our people. It was through the oppression of the oppressor, and through the religion he gave us, that our ears were opened. Esau is not poor. They are rich through robbery, and that continues to this day. We are a people robbed and spoiled and hid in prison houses, as Isaiah 42 says, and it is being played out in real time.

Just because you are not in the prison system doesn't mean you are not in captivity. Deuteronomy 28:15-68 applies to us: the Lord gave us the warning, we didn't take heed, and the curses are in full effect. The 13th Amendment was supposed to end slavery, but its clause, except as punishment for crime, made the loophole that fills the prisons with our people for free labor. Slavery was never abolished; it evolved. They framed mischief and made it law, like the throne of iniquity that “frameth mischief by a law.” A warden speaks of a young man's sweat equity instead of the death penalty, the same spirit as the Willie Lynch letter: don't kill him, it's not good economics.

This is still the land of our captivity, and the enemy got crafty with us. But in that oppression the Lord opened our ears. We were deaf and now we hear discipline; we were blind and now we see. We are not supposed to be at rest in this land. Your 9-to-5 is not your purpose; your purpose is to keep his commandments, remember that you are called and requested of God, and magnify his law upon the earth.

precepts.label: Isaiah 48:17
precepts.why:
“O my God, I trust in thee: let me not be ashamed, let not mine enemies triumph over me.” Then: “Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.” Look at what David is asking for: lead me and teach me.

Isaiah shows how God answers that: “Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.” He leads you by the way, in the direction you should go.

And God leads through the prophets he sends, and many of them were killed. People hate the word of God so much that they want to kill us. That's why it says be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. The brothers go out to teach and get guns pulled on them, just for reading the Bible, while dudes drive by selling crack, fentanyl, whatever they sell. Guns pulled on us by Christian folk. That's why the church can't be stood: church is full of crap.

So are we the enemies because we tell the people the truth? No. You're just simple and you don't want correction. We are going to do our job and teach you the good and the right way, and keep our hands clean. What you do with it is on you. Either repent, or die in your sins.

precepts.label: Isaiah 35:3-4
precepts.why:
David prays, “raise me up, that I may requite them”: raise me up the third day, so I can get vengeance on the traitor who ate of my bread. Isaiah tells the faithful to hold on for that vengeance: “Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.”

In every IUIC school some brothers may be weak and feeble, spiritually. Build them up. You have to build your inner circle up, loyal and faithful brothers who know the scriptures and fear God, and then have a circle outside of that of trustworthy, loyal men, so that when Jacob's trouble comes you don't all fall.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”. Brothers and sisters, be strong, because at times you might get afraid, but the Lord has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

Then: “behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” We must believe that our God will come with vengeance. A recompence is a requital, the same word as “that I may requite them” in the psalm: an appropriate return for wrongdoing.

Isaiah 47 shows that vengeance on Babylon: “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”. All these fake Christians talking about America being a Christian society: their nakedness is uncovered by the word of God, and all their shameful deeds are revealed. “I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” Christ is not coming back meeting them as a man. So strengthen the weak, fear not, and wait on the God who comes with recompence to save us.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 19:13-15
precepts.why:
The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

precepts.label: Proverbs 18:24
precepts.why:
Why is a friend's admonishment the same matter as speaking against your brother? Because friend and brother are synonymous. Proverbs explains it: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

There are some friends that are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50:20 says “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”, the slander lands on the friend who admonished you as much as on your own blood.

A man that has friends must show himself friendly, not turn on the friend who corrects him. And God will not keep silence forever: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” That is Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. “and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God”, and the salvation is only to Israel.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:11
precepts.why:
Solomon was knocked down, and David, the man after the Lord's own heart, was knocked down. Did they stay down? No. We are not in the business of staying down; we get knocked down and keep going. Satan tells us to stay down, and some brothers and sisters want you to stay down, but that is not what God said. “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” That is what God is looking for.

So what do we pray when Satan knocks us down? David prayed it: “Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” We pray that the Lord does not remove his Holy Spirit from us, because that is what keeps us standing.

“Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.” You have to look at the truth with a joyful and glad heart, because you cannot live without it; it is part of your system, your life. Where else can you go? We do not give up our position; we pray that the Lord keeps strengthening us.

“Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” When we get back up, our job is to teach, because we have been through the trial and tribulation and understand what it takes. We go right back to the business we left off, teaching our people their transgressions so they do not fall into what we fell into. Do we give that up to go sit on the couch, or sit in the back and puff up on evil?

Nobody sees the prayer, the crying at night, the tears when you are home alone thinking, I could have done better. That is the broken and contrite heart God will not despise. Tell Satan to bring it on. With a position or without it, be the same: a trooper. And when a brother is knocked down, do not applaud it; fast and pray for him, because he is still fighting the same battle you are, and your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his.

precepts.label: Judith 5:11
precepts.why:
The psalm says of the nations, “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” Who are God's people? We are God's people. And Judith shows one of their crafty counsels from the beginning: “Therefore the king of Egypt rose up against them, and dealt subtilly with them, and brought them low with labouring in brick, and made them slaves.”

That is one of their crafty counsels: we are going to work them to death. Today many of our people are working two big jobs, living paycheck to paycheck, too poor to stop working. It is happening even more with Trump in office. There is no middle class; that thing is gone. You can't work for a living wage and survive out here.

There was a time, and some of you older people understand, when you could have a job delivering milk or eggs, or work in a post office, and buy a home on one salary. Not no more. People with full-time jobs making $50,000 a year in LA are homeless, living in storage units.

They said, we have to find ways to keep the children of Israel under our foot. If we can't get them in religion, we will get them in the workforce. If not the workforce, gangs; if not gangs, porn; we will turn them into criminals. That is the crafty counsel of the nations, confederate with one consent, to cut Israel off from being a nation. In this world, all we have got is us.

classes.title: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra, “I will liken my judgment unto a ring: like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” God's judgment goes round like a ring, a wheel. It comes around without fail, the last no slower than the first.

The scriptures say God shall be known in his judgments. So when Deuteronomy says that when we sin we will find ourselves back in captivity, in slavery and in prison houses, and we look around and see those conditions, his judgment stands. It is sure, and his prophecies are fulfilled. That is how we show that God is here: so take heed and fear God.

That is the frame for Psalms 94:20: “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” The 13th Amendment abolished slavery except as punishment for crime. Within fifteen years the Southern states were imprisoning black Americans at ten times the rate of whites; they made loitering and vagrancy felonies and leased the convicts out for forced labor. Today prison labor makes billions while inmates earn cents an hour. They framed mischief by a law and misled us with democracy and freedom. Slavery did not end; it evolved.

A former warden testified that a young defendant should get life without parole instead of death because the prison could use him: he is young, he is healthy, we need that sweat equity. That is the Willie Lynch letter: beat him within an inch of his life but don't kill him, because it is not good for economics.

The throne of iniquity has no fellowship with Christ: not their holidays, not their man-made religions, and no, the president is not God. Some people do need to be locked up if they rob and steal. But the judgment keeps turning like a ring, and what we institute is keeping God's commandments, so that you stay far from all of that.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:48
precepts.why:
Christ says it plainly: “Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” You see it right there in red. For those taking notes, those new to this, those still on the fence: this is Christ himself speaking.

That is the wondrous thing the psalmist asks to behold: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” When I keep God’s commandments, the wondrous thing I see out of them is that he wants me to be like him. God gave law so that we can be like unto him, perfect as our Father in heaven is perfect.

Those eyes are not only the bodily eyes. They are the spiritual eyes, the insight to see this word and the situation we are in, and to understand that it is all spiritual. That is why we have to delve into the scriptures and meditate, so that we can behold the wondrous things out of God’s law, and after we understand and observe, apply it and be like our Father.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:2
precepts.why:
This is what Christ’s words meant in the Old Testament. The Lord told Moses: “Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the Lord your God am holy.” God is holy, and he says, you shall be holy.

Holiness is us coming into perfection. That is the wondrous thing out of God’s law in Psalms 119:18: the law is given so that his children can become like him.

What makes us perfect? Read on in Psalms 19. “The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.” The sun, the moon and the stars prove there must be a God; but how much more should you show him in your conversation and your actions, by not sinning? Then: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The law is perfect because God’s laws are his ways, his habits, and he gave them unto his children. It converts us from darkness into light, from the power of Satan unto the power of God, for the redemption of our souls.

Then: “the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were simple, lost through slavery and oppression, calling ourselves anything but who we are. Coming back to understanding that we are the Israelites, and striving for perfection by keeping the law, is our souls being converted. And you cannot come to perfection without trials: gold is tried in the fire.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:16
precepts.why:
Wisdom says, “Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold.” What are those riches? Colossians shows it: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.”

The riches we are looking for are not money, though people think they are. We need the durable riches, which is wisdom: the word of Christ dwelling in us richly. And this is what we are supposed to do with it: teach and admonish one another.

God says, I am giving it to you. But you are walking in hypocrisy, distracted by covetousness, and a man’s life does not consist of the abundance of what he has. That was not their kingdom at that point, and all of this is coming to an end anyway. God has something far better than what you are looking at, and you are about to throw it away for this world.

Now you understand what the scripture is saying, so you have no excuse. Much is given, so much is required, and the one who knew will be beaten with many stripes. So I have to walk in that, stand in that space and be that, or get ready to get beat. The durable riches of Proverbs 8 are the word living in us richly, and they have to be walked in.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:37
precepts.why:
“In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Wanteth not means it does not lack: where there are many words, sin is never missing. Christ gave the rule for our speech: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay, and everything else is evil.

How many times do you hear it: brother, listen, stop talking. Brother, I am trying to help you, stop talking. You think you are saying something deep, and you are burying yourself. He just cannot stop talking.

Take the brother at work who handed his phone to a girl while the other brother stepped to the back. Asked why, he said it was nothing. Then it was business. What business do you have with her, when we just walked into this place? Nah, it was nothing. Now you are repeating yourself. That is the multitude of words, the over-explaining, and it gave him away. Just by seeing the phone the other brother knew something was not right, and there was more behind it.

That is the ears and the eyes being exercised. Your ears have to be tuned to the subtleties in speech, and a man's face will tell you what is really going on, not what he says. The heart takes what it has seen and heard, processes it and comes to a conclusion; to discern between good and evil you have to be spiritual. Speech reveals the thoughts formed in the heart, so the one who refrains his lips and keeps his yea to yea and his nay to nay is wise.

precepts.label: Proverbs 21:16
precepts.why:
“Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.” A man keeps rehearsing the same sin over and over, and in his own eyes he thinks he is walking right. When you keep doing the same thing over and over, you are getting further away from God. Watch what the same chapter says: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

You are wandering away from God. You keep doing the same thing over and over and over and wonder why life is not working out for you. This is what spiritual men and women are supposed to examine: things aren't working right right now; could it be that you have a secret life?

They thought sacrifice was going to absolve them, but “To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.” We repent to the Lord, Lord, we're sorry, then go back and do the same thing again: we're not really sorry. We set up prayers and fasts and return to the same behavior, because we don't really understand the fear of God. To know right and still do wrong is presumptuous sin, and we've all been guilty of it. But there has to be a day we stop, or we won't receive the kingdom.

So we all want the kingdom? Then we have to change on this end. We can't wait and think we'll become somebody different in the kingdom. Bring forth fruits meet for repentance, or remain with the congregation of the dead.

thread.label: Proverbs 23:17-19
thread.text: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long.

classes.title: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.label: Proverbs 23:33
precepts.why:
“Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way”: guard your heart and your mind in these commandments and these laws. Jump down the same chapter and see what happens to the heart that is not guided: “Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.”

Your eyes behold an evil woman, and your heart begins to utter. Does your heart utter anything? You utter from your mouth. So your eye is connected to your mind, and your mind is connected to your mouth. You see, you entertain, and then you begin to talk: hey, let me get your number, what's going on? Now you're talking, and you have no self-control over your members. Eye, mind, mouth. Out of the abundance of your heart your mouth speaks. No control, and then you're caught up.

It is the same road envy travels in verse 17, “Let not thine heart envy sinners”. Young people see the rapper's house, the girls, the car; the eyes instruct the mind, and the mind begins to envy: I want that, I want to be part of that. When you entertain it, you're telling God, that's what I choose, and this book isn't important. That is why we went into captivity: we did not serve the Lord with joyfulness and gladness of heart for the abundance of all things.

So guide thine heart in the way. Turn the eyes away before the mind takes hold and the mouth follows; that is self-control, and it keeps you in the fear of the Lord all the day long.

thread.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: John 14:8-9
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the son that is given “The everlasting Father.” Most Christians, and even some Israelites, cannot explain that, because they have not figured out that the everlasting Father in the Old Testament was Christ. They say we always spoke to the Father. No, you did not speak to the Father; you spoke to Christ. That is why he is called the everlasting Father. John 14 is a precept for it.

“Philip saith unto him, Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us.” See Christ’s response: “Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?”

Yes, Christ looks like his Father. But what is he actually telling Philip? I created you. I am your Father, your everlasting Father. You were brought forth through me.

Remember, Christ is the only begotten of the Father. That means the Father created only Christ, and then told Christ to create everything else. So when Isaiah names the child born unto us “The mighty God, The everlasting Father”, it is because everything that exists was brought forth through him. That is why Philip, who had been with him so long, should have known him.

precepts.label: John 1:1-3
precepts.why:
In case anyone is still confused about why Christ is called “The everlasting Father”, John 1 settles it. We have to shake the Christian thoughts.

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Christ was in the beginning with God, and he was God. “The same was in the beginning with God.” God is a plural there.

Then the part that matters: “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ, and without Christ was not any thing made that was made. The Father only begat Christ, and through Christ everything else was created.

That is why he said to Philip, “Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip?” I created all of this. That is too heavy for a Negro, because you have Baptist on your mind and Catholic in your head. It was hard for us in the beginning too, but the Most High has shown us. Let it marinate.

So the child born and the son given in Isaiah 9:6, with the government upon his shoulder, is the same one who made all things: the Word, the mighty God, the everlasting Father.

precepts.label: Matthew 13:31-32
precepts.why:
“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Christ explains that increase in Matthew 13: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.” If you grew up in the city you may not know what a mustard seed looks like; it is one of the smallest of all seeds.

“but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.” When it is grown: that is the increase of his government. It starts small. What we have here is small. We may think we have a lot, but this is nothing yet; we are still at the mustard seed stage.

And the kingdom of heaven is a government, not a church group. That is why it behooves us to learn God’s laws, commandments and statutes: to set up a government you need everything that makes a community, and God’s laws are going to filter everything for us. Right now we think small. God says think bigger. A house? Bigger. Property? Bigger. The world is ours, and for the world to be ours we have to be able to set all of that up.

Think how the Most High uses something as small as the human mind. As a man thinketh, so is he. Everything you lay your eyes on, every object and invention, was a thought first. We shortchange ourselves with doubt, but that is not what God made. Untapped greatness is waiting to bud; remove the doubt and the fear and let the Lord work on that head.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:12-21
precepts.why:
The mustard seed government is small now, and we think small. Compare what God did for Solomon with where we are today.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” Solomon learned wisdom and gave it out freely, and that is what we are doing today: we don’t hide the riches of the wisdom of God. “For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.” If we use this wisdom we become the friends of God. And it comes from learning, not once but daily; that is what the classes every day are about.

“For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements.” You might say you know how the world was made. You don’t: what elements make the air, what elements were made for the sun? Solomon understood that. He knew “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”, from Adam to the second coming of Christ. He knew “the alterations of the turning of the sun, and the change of seasons”, “The circuits of years, and the positions of stars.”

“The natures of living creatures”: Esau puts cameras on animals, even in their butts, to learn how they defecate, trying to get on Solomon’s level with all that freakiness. Solomon knew “the furies of wild beasts”, “the violence of winds”, the tornadoes and storms, “the reasonings of men”, “the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”, which herb is for what, and “all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.”

We are not even on Solomon’s level yet. We need the Lord to open our minds up to get there, and when he does we will be on that level and greater. That is what the mustard seed is about: we start small and it grows. This is the beginning of that government.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 23:5-6
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the government shall be upon his shoulder, “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice.” Jeremiah says the same: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch.” That righteous Branch is Christ.

“and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” See what he is going to do: execute judgment and justice in the earth. The nations don’t want that. Some of us in here may not want that either: I don’t want no justice and judgment, hell no. Yes, it is coming anyway.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

So the throne of David in Isaiah 9 is the reign of this King, the Branch raised unto David. The increase of his government is a kingdom of judgment and justice, of law and order, and in his days Judah is saved and Israel dwells safely. That is why we learn God’s laws now: it is the government we are going to live under.

thread.text: The burden of the desert of the sea. As whirlwinds in the south pass through; so it cometh from the desert, from a terrible land.

classes.title: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:28-45
precepts.why:
Isaiah sees “the burden of the desert of the sea”: “the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth.” That is America, which invites you to a peace talk and then bombs your country, as it did Iran, and now tells every nation to take the deal: only white folks can have nuclear weapons, no weapons for you brown people. “Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media”: Iran, Pakistan, India, that whole section. Right now they are in a sighing period, bases destroyed and generals killed by drones, building up their arsenal and waiting. Then the burden upon Arabia, the sons of Ishmael, and “all the glory of Kedar shall fail.” Ezra shows how it all comes together.

“Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east: Where the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots.” Turkey, which is part of NATO, is making a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a NATO of the Arab nations, because Erdogan hates the Israelis so much. When Israel bombed Qatar, the Muslim world called an emergency summit, and Saudi Arabia called for revenge. “Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Carmanians are Iran, joining the Arabs, and the land of the Assyrians here is the Israelis.

“And then shall the dragons have the upper hand, remembering their nature.” Right now the Arabs are kissing America's butt, but they will remember their nature. Genesis 16 gives it: Ishmael “will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.” Wild enough to run into a crowded room with C4 strapped to his chest for 72 virgins. His hand against every man means you have no friends among them: they are true nationalists, and all twelve princes dwell together through that region.

It is only Black people that are not nationalists. We love everybody, we have to be friends with everybody, and meanwhile we are put to death left and right. Stop being stupid, men. A nationalist loves his nation and his people; that is the greatest commandment, love God and love your brother. Every nation loves its own. Christ was a nationalist: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And now Ibrahim Traoré is uniting Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, the most docile nations; the spirit of life is coming into them through the brothers teaching and preaching in Africa.

“And if they shall turn themselves, conspiring together in great power to persecute them, Then these shall be troubled” … “and shall flee. And from the land of the Assyrians shall the enemy besiege them, and consume some of them.” All the Arab nations conspiring together against the Israelis, just as we saw in the clip.

“Behold clouds from the east and from the north unto the south” … “full of wrath and storm.” The east is Asia, China and North Korea; the north is Russia, Turkey and Europe; the south is the Arabs and Africa; the clouds are their ships. “They shall smite down a great multitude of stars upon the earth, even their own star”: missiles, like the ones the Iron Dome shoots down. “And blood shall be from the sword unto the belly, And dung of men unto the camel’s hough.” Then “great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west”: the west is America and Canada.

Then “they shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star.” That is different from the stars before: the horrible star is the ICBM. With it, “Fire, and hail, and flying swords”, the conventional missiles. “And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid” … “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, like the kings of the earth in Revelation 18 standing afar off, crying that in one hour her judgment is come. Ezra 15:60 even shows them returning to Babylon that was destroyed: the air force and navy still fighting from a base that is gone.

That is what Isaiah's watchman saw: “Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground.” Fallen twice, because the Israelis over there fall too. Cesare Borgia, Santa Claus, the Thanksgiving turkey, the Easter bunny, the Greek statues everywhere: all of it finished. It is Bible prophecy unfolding before our eyes, and while it happens, get yourselves together, brothers and sisters.

precepts.label: Micah 2:11
precepts.why:
Isaiah prophesies against the elders and rulers of his time: “they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine.” People read that and think these men were getting drunk. That is not what it is talking about. Micah shows what the wine is.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” The wine and strong drink are the falsehoods and the lies. It is not the priests and prophets actually getting drunk and teaching; it is them pushing doctrines.

Read Isaiah again with that: they have erred through doctrine, lies and falsehoods, and are out of the way of the Lord. “they err in vision, they stumble in judgment”: they do not teach correctly; it is their erroneous doctrine. “For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.”

So if the priests and prophets are that wicked, whom will God teach knowledge? “them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts”: those raised on the word of God, the Old and New Testament, who learn it “precept must be upon precept”, “line upon line”, “here a little, and there a little”, not by commentary and the doctrine of the oppressor.

And that same strong drink is the refuge of the rulers in verse 15: “we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” I teach everybody can be saved, I teach he is not Esau, the white man will protect me, the scourge will pass me by. Micah’s prophet of wine and strong drink is exactly the prophet this people wants.

thread.text: But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine

precepts.label: Isaiah 47:12
precepts.why:
Babylon's destruction comes “in a moment in one day”, and the Lord gives the reason: “for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments.” There was sorcery used upon our people in America, and then America used that same thing on all the nations.

That is why your uncle and your auntie won't repent after you accepted Christianity. That is witchcraft, used to keep you in the state of mind you are in. It is the pattern of every captivity: from the Assyrian captivity to the Babylonian, from the Medes and the Persians to the Greeks and to Rome, and now we are in America. All the nations have always used enchantments and witchcraft against us to keep us in darkness, and Satan is dealing with them.

The word enchantment means magic, witchcraft, sorcery, wizardry, necromancy, conjuration, hypnotism, mesmerism, voodoo, charms, spells, incantations, mojo. Remember coming out of Egypt, when the magicians were doing their things? Those magicians are who call themselves scientists today, with different titles under that name. They are the witches of this earth. Hypnotism is like the movie Get Out: our people have been sinking, and it is time to help them come out. America did not use only words against us. It used every witchcraft and every voodoo it could find, and the Catholic church is part of that foolishness.

Then the Lord dares them: “Stand now with thine enchantments, and with the multitude of thy sorceries, wherein thou hast laboured from thy youth.” America has been dealing with the devil from its youth up. “If so be thou shalt be able to profit, if so be thou mayest prevail.” The Lord is saying: since you have practiced these things from your youth, let me see if you will prevail against me. Let me see if that little nuke, that robot that is half a man, all that witchcraft and all the media you have through the earth, can stop what I am bringing into this earth.

We saw it when America was trying to attack and the Lord raised up a storm that destroyed helicopters and airplanes. They don't understand the prophecy. These things are already written, and no man can change them. The nuclear weapons every nation holds are not going to sit on a shelf like extra paint; an ICBM can reach Washington in under half an hour, and what Isaiah and Jeremiah spoke of exists in our time.

That is why we are out here teaching and telling our people to repent. We see what is coming. The same way God destroyed the first world with a flood, he is going to destroy this world with fire, and no sorcery or weapon can stop what God has written.

thread.text: Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God.

precepts.label: Job 8:8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 51:20 says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. What other people on the planet are at the head of every corner on the streets? That's us: in Miami, in the Bronx, in all the hoods and all the ghettos throughout the whole earth. We fainted, we are hid in prison houses, and we are on every corner. They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs, uncs and OGs, but that ain't your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings?

So the Lord says, “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors. When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. It is no longer, I'm a YN: we have young prophets amongst us. We are raising up our sons and daughters, young men, teens and young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What our fathers went through was written for our learning, to increase our faith. When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives us a guide for how we need to be today. That's called legacy.

How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. We are going to have to get back to that, and who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:28
precepts.why:
“For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity.” Our hands in the black and brown community are defiled with blood. In Joliet a young man, twenty-three years old, shot to death his own mother, his aunt, his uncle, his bedridden brother and his three sisters, killed another man and shot one more, and then shot himself. That's trauma right there, and the law explains it: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

The Lord shall smite thee with madness: meaning our people are insane. No rhyme, no reason to what they do or why they do it. That's being smitten with madness. We have generational curses. Three teens on a thirty-hour spree of armed robberies and the murder of a churchgoing man; a woman charged with stabbing and killing a three-year-old boy, appearing in court laughing and smiling: that is stricken with madness.

The Bible says, thou shalt not kill, and we are not taught that in church, so some of us grow up with a hateful and murderous spirit on us. No matter how bad, insulting or degrading these videos are, they are filtered through the Bible, showing the stage and state of where we are today, and it is still proof that we are the children of Israel under the curses. The Bible ain't the white man's book. The Bible is our book.

That is why the Lord's hand is not shortened and his ear is not heavy, and still he does not save: “your iniquities have separated between you and your God.”

precepts.label: Revelation 13:9-10
precepts.why:
“None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth.” You might say, that's not right; our people are in the street all the time crying, no justice, no peace. But the justice our people want is called money. They don't want the justice of the Bible. Here is God's justice: “If any man have an ear, let him hear. He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.”

Now that's justice. And you know what our people say? No, you hate the white man. They know what the scripture means: the one who led into slavery going into slavery, the one who killed with the sword being put to death by the sword. And they say, no, we don't want that kind of justice. We want money, money, money.

That is Isaiah 59:4: none calling for God's justice. They cry for justice in the streets, but when the justice of God is read to them, they call it hateful.

precepts.label: Psalms 89:14
precepts.why:
“Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.” God's throne is all about justice and judgment. That's exactly what the world doesn't want.

“nor any pleadeth for truth”: they are not pleading for God's truth. The families of our brothers and sisters put to death unjustly, Sandra Bland and the rest, want the truth regarding their case, but they don't want God's truth as a whole. We may march with them and support them, but there is no internal change: they are mad at the white man and still celebrating Christmas and the white man's holidays. “be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.” If I used to celebrate Easter, now I celebrate Passover. They are making a conscious effort not to change.

The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, the habitation of his throne. That is why the world, which cries for justice, will be angry when it comes.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:18
precepts.why:
Everybody says, I can't wait until Jesus comes back. Let's see what the Bible says: “And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come.” All these nations, countries and religious organizations say they want the Messiah to return, and the Bible prophesies they will be angry.

Why are they angry? Because “Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne.” The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, and the nations don't want that. Many of those nations are living on stolen land, like America. This is stolen land. They are lying when they say they can't wait. Christ's wrath is coming; he's not coming to hand out lollipops and hugs and kisses.

“and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great.” You know what that reward is? Power. He's going to give his servants power.

“and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.” That's them. They say the aerosols in the black and brown community are destroying the ozone layer, not their rockets and missiles. All that climate change global BS: they are the ones destroying the earth, digging up and sucking out the oil that is meant to lubricate the tectonic plates, and then they wonder why the earthquakes are happening. They know it, and that's why they will be angry at his return. None calleth for the justice of God.
