precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 5:15-23
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59 ends with the Lord seeing “that there was no man”, no intercessor, so his own arm brought salvation: Christ “put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing.” “The Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob”: not all nations. And his covenant is his spirit upon us and his words in our mouth, and in our children's mouths, and our children's children's, for ever. Wisdom of Solomon shows what that Redeemer brings.

“But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High.” There is no death to the righteous. If you are in this truth keeping the commandments in the faith of Christ, you live forever; our brothers and sisters whose bodies returned to the dust, those spirits are coming back. We have to believe that.

“Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord’s hand.” The glorious kingdom shall be on earth: that is New Jerusalem. The crown is the one in 2 Esdras 2:42-45: we are going to get crowned with power. “For with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.”

“He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour”: Christ is coming back for war. “And make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies”: that leviathan is going to come out and attack those bastards on the navy. “He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate”, the same as we read in Isaiah 59, “and true judgment instead of an helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. His severe wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the unwise.”

“Then shall the right aiming thunderbolts go abroad; and from the clouds, as from a well drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark.” Those weapons won't miss; that lightning won't miss. “And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow”, like in the time of Joshua, “and the water of the sea shall rage against them”, tsunamis, “and the floods shall cruelly drown them. Yea, a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storm shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.”

That is what we are waiting for: the second coming of Christ. And God would not be just to let the nations off the hook; if he punished his own people, America, England, Japan and Australia will not be unpunished. So while we wait, we must be preparing our hearts, our minds and our souls.

thread.label: Isaiah 59:5-8
thread.text: They hatch cockatrice’ eggs, and weave the spider’s web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: Matthew 3:7-8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59:5 says “They hatch cockatrice’ eggs”, and a cockatrice is like a poisonous snake. Put together everything from verses two to four, the iniquities that separated us from our God, the hands defiled with blood, the lips that have spoken lies, and this is what comes of it: “he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper.” The eggs that are crushed are the kids that come out: a little baby snake. They produce evil followers.

Many years ago at a community meeting a black woman screamed at the police that they were selling drugs in her building and nobody was doing anything. The police set up a sting and locked up two dudes putting drugs in the mailboxes: her own sons. Then she came back saying it was false, with them on video. These are the eggs, the snake eggs coming out.

John the Baptist saw the same thing: “But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers”. That is the same thing Isaiah was talking about. “who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”.

A generation of vipers cannot just say it repents. You have to bring forth God's commandments in application; that is what proves your repentance.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:34
precepts.why:
Now Christ is speaking to them: “O generation of vipers”. That goes back to Isaiah 59, the cockatrice' eggs that break out into a viper. Christ called them vipers, and John the Baptist called them vipers. And their children are little snakes too.

“how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What is in the heart comes out of the mouth. A generation of vipers cannot speak good things, because what fills their heart is evil.

That is Isaiah 59 again. Before verse 5, verse 3 said our lips have spoken lies and our tongue perverseness. The lips speak lies and the tongue perverseness because the heart is full of iniquity, and the eggs they hatch are the same kind as the ones who laid them.

precepts.label: Isaiah 65:2
precepts.why:
“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. See what our people do: they walk after their own thoughts. They don't give a damn what the Bible says; I do what I want to do.

And their thoughts are the white man's thoughts. Our people follow all these man-made religions, and they don't teach God's laws, his commandments, his statutes. We ain't got to keep no laws, because that is what all these white people were teaching: don't keep no laws.

So what do you get? Those vipers hatch eggs, and what comes out? Little vipers, little snakes. Your son, little Tyrone, is a snake, and your daughter, little Chenique, was a snake too. That is what God is saying in Isaiah 59:5, and it is why verse 7 says “their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity”: a rebellious people walking after their own thoughts.

precepts.label: Job 8:13-15
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59 says they “weave the spider’s web” and “Their webs shall not become garments”. Job explains the spider's web. “So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish: Whose hope shall be cut off”, because they are hypocrites, “and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.”

Their trust shall be as a spider's web: you get tangled up in that thing, and that spider comes out and bites you and eats you up.

“He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.” Your house won't stand. A people who forget God weave their webs and lean on what they built, but it cannot cover them or hold them up. That is why Isaiah 59:6 goes on, “neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:1-2
precepts.why:
Isaiah 59:6 says “neither shall they cover themselves with their works”, and Isaiah 30 shows the covering they use instead. “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me”: they are looking for counsel, but not from God. “and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit”, not according to the Bible, “that they may add sin to sin”.

“That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth”. At that time it was actual Egypt, but today it's America, spiritual Egypt. They have not asked the prophets what the Bible says. They go “to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” America ain't the real Egypt, but it is the shadow of Egypt, and our people trust in it.

That is why the act of violence is in their hands. A cruise line banned passengers for life over a brawl in the buffet; graduation ceremonies break out into fights with families arrested, a day of celebration turned into chaos. Our people have made crooked paths for themselves, following the Democratic or the Republican party, the cross and the white Jesus, and whosoever goes therein shall not know peace.

thread.label: Isaiah 59:9-15
thread.text: Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:29
precepts.why:
“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men.” We got eyes, but we act like we ain't got none. We act like what we just saw didn't happen. The curse said it would be so: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

We are like blind people, but we have eyes. We see we're not prospering as a people. We see we're under constant oppression as a people. But we act like we don't see it, because oppression has become so normal to us; it's our everyday life.

It's high noon, but in our minds we are so spiritually blind it is like night for us. “we are in desolate places as dead men”: that's the black and brown community, desolate places, our people like the walking dead. Isaiah 59 is Deuteronomy 28:29 in real time.

That is why verse 9 says, “Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.” We want to live filthy lives, evil lives, violent lives, and then expect justice from God. It don't work like that. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 11:12-13
precepts.why:
There is a difference between being spiritually slow and being spiritually dead. “we are in desolate places as dead men,” but Sirach shows what the nation needs: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” We usually read it as an individual, but think about it on a bigger scale. You might say this is Joe or Bob. No, this is us.

Slow, needing help, lacking ability, full of poverty: that is our people. “yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,” and lifted up his head from misery, so that many that saw it marvelled at him.

The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up. It will be such a shock that this low, degenerate race of people is now going to rule the earth. We lack the ability now; it is the Lord's eye that sets us up from our low estate.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:20-21
precepts.why:
“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel; think of it as whatever IUIC school you come from. Every camp leader, the head of the sanctuary, must be able to identify the gold brothers and the silver brothers, the gold sisters and silver sisters, and also look through the school and say, this brother and this sister is earth, this one is wood.

If you can't discern that, you'll have problems in the school, putting people in positions that don't fit them. Marcus Garvey had his ships and put his best friends over them, and they didn't know how to run a ship: one crashed, one went to his girlfriend's house, and he lost it all because of friendship. Shake the friendship appointments. Who is best qualified? Who knows what they're doing? A dummy who doesn't study set up as a school leader, and all hell breaks loose. If sanctuary leaders have no discernment, they are spiritually blind and destined for ruin.

Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need more time to grow. Fine; don't put them in that position yet if others are better qualified. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits. They see this truth not as a government, not as the mustard seed of a government, but as a social club, dancing every new moon and confused when it comes to God's work. That is how a people groping like the blind becomes vessels unto honour.

precepts.label: John 3:18-21
precepts.why:
The voices of our people conceive and utter from the heart words of falsehood, lies on top of lies. Christ answers: “He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.” If you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned; if you believe not, you're not even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Christ is that light that came into the world, and men love darkness, sin, rather than light, Christ and keeping the commandments. It didn't change from Isaiah to John; it's the same thing: “we wait for light, but behold obscurity.”

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ, they hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: have no other gods before me, bow down to no graven image, remember the Sabbath, honour your father and your mama, thou shalt not kill. They don't want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest. What am I? Lord, show me.

precepts.label: Amos 5:10
precepts.why:
“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” If you depart from evil by repenting, you make yourself a prey to everybody around you; everybody around you hates your guts now. Amos says the same thing: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

That includes some of your own mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers. They hate the one who rebukes and abhor the one who speaks uprightly, because “truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter.”

“and the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.” There was no true judgment in the earth. The one who departs from evil is hated for it, and the Lord sees it.

thread.label: Isaiah 59:16-21
thread.text: And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him.

classes.title: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

thread.label: Isaiah 61:1-6
thread.text: The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the pri

classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted.” He has chosen and set apart every man here, all the captains, to preach good tidings to the meek. But how do you bind up a person that is broken? The brokenhearted are broken in the mind: suffering the curses without knowing the will of God. We are set apart to bind them up. What do we bind them with?

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” We bind up the testimony and seal the law in the minds of the people, because they are brokenhearted and their minds are broken. That is what we are called to do: to bind them to the laws of God.

And we show them why it is good. Look at our lives as the example of what it means to serve God and why it is good to serve him. That means we have to be sincere about it. How do we tell the people to touch not the unclean thing and then not live it ourselves? The one who was profitable to many but not to himself will be punished accordingly, because he knew better.

So the good tidings we proclaim with the law are these: if we repent and keep God's laws in sincerity and endure to the end, he will deliver us, and we will rule again, as we were made in his image to rule.

precepts.label: Isaiah 49:1-8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 says to “proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord”, and Isaiah 49 says it again: “Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages.” The acceptable year and the acceptable time: that is when we heal the broken heart and proclaim liberty to the captives.

“The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name. And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me; And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” We are supposed to glorify our God in this body.

“Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.” We go to stiff-necked, hard-hearted people who refuse to hear the word of God, but we still proclaim the day of the Lord to heal those minds and tell them there is an end to this: we will rule one day. He formed us from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” It may not appear that we are doing it, but when the numbers come in, it is a light thing he has given us, and he still charges us to raise up the children of Israel. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that goes back to Matthew 4, the Gentiles of Galilee. Our job is to bring salvation to the people and lead them back to him, and that is a great ministry.

“Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” … “and he shall choose thee.” Out of all of them, he is going to choose us. And unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: we want to be the faithful servant the Lord finds doing this work in sincerity, without deceit and without secret sins.

classes.title: America: Hammer of the Earth

thread.label: Jeremiah 2:21
thread.text: Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed: how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?

classes.title: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.label: Jeremiah 2:19
precepts.why:
“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”. The Lord planted us a noble vine: he gave us the commandments and the scriptures and made us elite, the top people on the planet earth, holy and right. “how then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” The Lord looked at us and said, wow, y'all degenerate.

How did we become that degenerate plant? Verse 19 tells us: “Thine own wickedness shall correct thee, and thy backslidings shall reprove thee”. That is how we became degenerate: our own wickedness. “know therefore and see that it is an evil thing and bitter, that thou hast forsaken the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not in thee, saith the Lord God of hosts.”

Are we feeling it now, brothers and sisters? Look at our conditions: the trauma, poverty, fatherlessness and broken families, the curse of Deuteronomy 28 passed from one generation to the next. That is the bitterness of having forsaken the Lord.

So our mission is the one in Maccabees: “Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” We have to restore the decayed state of our people: learn the word of God, apply it to our lives, and go out and teach our people, so the degenerate plant becomes the noble vine again.

thread.text: The word that the Lord spake against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans by Jeremiah the prophet.

classes.title: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.label: Luke 5:36-39
precepts.why:
“My people hath been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray, they have turned them away on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their restingplace.” The shepherds, the pastors, lead our people from one religion to another, and they have forgotten their restingplace, the word of God. Pastors charged with rape and child abuse, a pastor arrested on counts of rape of girls thirteen and fifteen, two pastors charged in the murder for hire of a blind, mentally disabled man for insurance money: that is how the shepherds have caused them to go astray. Yet Christians do not want to change, just as the Pharisees did not want to change.

Christ told them a parable: “No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agreeth not with the old.” Christ is the piece of new garment; the new covenant was being ushered in and they were not ready for it. It agreed not with the old covenant: animal sacrifice was replaced by the sacrifice of Christ.

“And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish. But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.” The new wine is the new covenant in Christ. The new bottles are us being born again: new creatures, new men, new women.

“No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.” That is how the Pharisees and scribes felt about Christ's teaching, and so it is today with Christians and the true teaching of Christ and the Israelites. Our people like their old ways and old traditions, and when we bring them the new covenant in Christ by keeping the commandments, they say, I don't want that. So “their adversaries said, We offend not, because they have sinned against the Lord, the habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers.”

thread.label: Jeremiah 50:21-46
thread.text: Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: waste and utterly destroy after them, saith the Lord, and do according to all that I have commanded thee.

classes.title: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:5
precepts.why:
Jeremiah 50 ends with the hammer of the whole earth broken: “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”. The least of the flock is the so-called Israelis, that tiny speck in the midst of the brown and black nations. They bomb Qatar during peace talks, cry help us, and America comes to their rescue. “surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them”: America desolate, and little Israel over there wiped out too. “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved, and the cry is heard among the nations.”

Then chapter 51 turns to us: “For Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts”. That means us. It might seem like we have been forsaken because we are down and out, at the bottom. But Israel has not been forsaken, because of the covenant the Lord made with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and he sent his Son Christ to die for our sins.

“though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.” Even in the midst of our sin he has not forsaken us. That is the same mercy the class read in Isaiah 14:1, the Lord will have mercy on Jacob and will yet choose Israel, and nobody has anything to say about it. He is not having mercy on all nations or pardoning all nations; while Babylon, the hammer, is broken, Israel and Judah are kept.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:41-49
precepts.why:
“How is Sheshach taken! and how is the praise of the whole earth surprised!” Sheshach is another name for Babylon. America is the praise of the whole earth; everybody has God bless America. “how is Babylon become an astonishment among the nations!” All the nations will be shocked when she goes down.

“The sea is come up upon Babylon: she is covered with the multitude of the waves thereof.” The sea is the nations. Ezekiel says it: “will cause many nations to come up against thee, as the sea causeth his waves to come up.” “Her cities are a desolation, a dry land, and a wilderness, a land wherein no man dwelleth, neither doth any son of man pass thereby.” That has not happened yet; it is yet to come.

“And I will punish Bel in Babylon”. Bel was a false god, and the Bel of today is Cesare Borgia, the god of Babylon. “and the nations shall not flow together any more unto him”: in Daniel 2 the last kingdom was a mix of all nations, and that is America. God will put an end to that. “yea, the wall of Babylon shall fall.”

“My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of the Lord.” Revelation 18:4 says the same: come out of her, that ye be not partakers of her sins and receive not of her plagues, those nuclear bombs. Come out of Christmas, Easter, Kwanzaa, Memorial Day and all the foolishness done here, and return to the one true God by keeping his commandments.

“And lest your heart faint, and ye fear for the rumour”. Do not give up. A rumour is something heard and talked about that has not occurred yet: World War III and Armageddon are the rumour now, the wars and rumours of wars of Matthew 24:6. Then “violence in the land, ruler against ruler.” “Then the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for Babylon: for the spoilers shall come unto her from the north”, as the whole earth breaks forth into singing in Isaiah 14:7. “As Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the earth.”

thread.label: Ezekiel 18:1-3
thread.text: The word of the Lord came unto me again, saying,

classes.title: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.label: Ezekiel 18:14
precepts.why:
The proverb was, “The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”: the present generation punished for the offences of their forefathers. The people were prone to plead their innocence: listen, I am this way because my father was this way. But the Lord said, “ye shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel.” I am not letting you use the fact that you have been through intergenerational trauma, or that your fathers weren't right.

“Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.” From here on out, you are not going to say, well, my daddy was wicked, so I am just going to be wicked by default. No, you are going to change it.

Verse 14 shows the son who does: “Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like”. The son sees everything his father did, considers it, and does not do the same. A son can see it and change.

So the proverb is broken by a son who looks at his father's ways with open eyes. The iniquity we were shapen in is real, but it is not a sentence we have to serve; the son who considers and does not do such like is the proof that it can be changed.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 18:19-20
precepts.why:
The people still asked, “Yet say ye, Why? doth not the son bear the iniquity of the father?” That is the sour grapes proverb again. The Lord answers: “When the son hath done that which is lawful and right, and hath kept all my statutes, and hath done them, he shall surely live. The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father”.

In other words, yes, intergenerational trauma is real. But do you just sit in it, or do you change? This son changed. If there is a son who changes and does what is right according to the Lord, he is not going to die, although his father will. Just because our fathers were wicked, just because our mothers didn't know God's laws and taught us evil, that is not an excuse to stay in this. That trauma is real; you must recognise it and move on from it.

“neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.” Each soul answers for itself.

And the Lord still has mercy on the sick. Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick”, and “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” That is every last one of us. Although we have been through trauma and traumatic experiences, we cannot use the excuse of what we have been through anymore. Christ has given us a clean slate, and the way to walk in it is to keep his statutes and do them.

thread.label: Ezekiel 36:24-28
thread.text: For I will take you from among the heathen, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land.

classes.title: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

precepts.label: Ezekiel 36:33-36
precepts.why:
Ezekiel 36:24-28 is the Lord changing us: gathered out of all countries, sprinkled with clean water, which is the commandments of God, given a new heart, a new mind, a new body, a new nervous system, with the stony, sinful heart that Adam had taken away. Then verse 33 shows what comes next: “Thus saith the Lord God; In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be builded.”

“And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say, This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden”. First the Lord changes you; now he changes the land to conform to you. The Lord made it for us; the world was made for us. But he can't give us Jerusalem the way it is supposed to be right now, because we are in the midst of sin.

So he says: let me remove the sin, let me cleanse you, let me give you a new heart, let me remove that weak, brittle body and give you immortality. Then he will command the land to transform into the garden of Eden. We are going right back to where we were in the beginning with our father Adam, and we are going to be with our father Adam again: his name is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah, in the same place.

“and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced, and are inhabited. Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the Lord build the ruined places, and plant that that was desolate: I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.” The nations will say, God is with these people. He has spoken it, and he will do it.

thread.label: Ezekiel 37:16-23
thread.text: Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the h

classes.title: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10-11
precepts.why:
When the voice told Peter, “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common”, Peter would have had to go to the Old Testament to explain what God had cleansed. He would go to Ezekiel 37: “I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” And whom was he gathering, and from where? “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”: they were living among the Gentiles, the nations. He gathers them, cleanses them, and takes the two kingdoms, the stick of Judah and the stick of Joseph in the hand of Ephraim, and makes them one.

Hosea shows the same joining: “Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” That is the two sticks becoming one in the Lord's hand.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The northern kingdom, cast out among the heathen and called not my people, would be called the sons of the living God again. That was the prophecy, and that is why Peter could not call those men common: the time had come, Peter, we have to gather them together, bring them together.

And guess what: that is happening now. It has been going on since back then until now. We are out in South America gathering God's people, out in Africa gathering God's people, and here in the States bringing God's people back together, Judah and Israel under one head.

precepts.label: Exodus 19:6
precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me”. What does that part mean, that thou shalt be no priest to me?

There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” A kingdom of priests. That is what Israel was called to be.

Go back to Hosea and it tells you why we lost it: “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”. That is the knowledge. Usually we jump over to Malachi 2:7, but the verse tells you right there: the knowledge is the law of God, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Because we forgot it, he rejected us from that priesthood.

That is why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, mentally and spiritually. The twelve tribes of Israel are a destroyed race. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. The black man and the brown man do have the ability, and many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they do not want us to have the capabilities.

thread.text: I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.

precepts.label: Additions to Esther 13:18
precepts.why:
“in their affliction they will seek me early.” God returns to his place, and our people have to seek him, but they have to be afflicted first. That is how our people are. And the afflictions are just starting. We have been getting killed in the street by police, but that ain't it; that is only the prelude to what is about to happen.

Esau is turning back the hands of the civil rights era right now, and that is good, because black people trust in their oppression. Memphis, maybe the blackest city in America, has been gerrymandered and carved up and parcelled out to the outskirts of the state so no black man can win a congressional seat there anymore, and it is happening in Texas and everywhere. An elected black congressman was hauled out by state troopers, protesting that he was an elected official and lawfully there. White guilt is out the window. Our people swear they are going to vote their way out of this, and they need the affliction, to see the devil for who he is.

In Esther's day: “All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” That is when our people are going to come: when death is before their eyes, they will cry earnestly and look for God. Right now they are still confused about who the devil is.

The church that once organized the community and planned the votes is silent while the civil rights laws are turned back, while our people are found hanged in 2026 with their organs taken out and it is called suicide. The only ones crying out about it are the Israelites. So it is our job to warn our people and bring them to repentance, and when they come with death before their eyes, we will show them what they are doing wrong and how to get right.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1-3
precepts.why:
Our people will cry earnestly when death is before their eyes, and Zephaniah says what to do before it comes: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” If you are seeking righteousness, you are admitting that you don't have it yet; you are walking in error and correcting it. So pray, Lord, show me where I am in error so I can fix it, so that when your decree brings forth I am lined up on the right side. That means when somebody is sent to tell you, this is wrong, you hear it and learn, because you don't want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

So when you come to the house of learning and somebody shows you your error, don't get mad and leave. Leaving means going back out there to face the fierce anger of God unprepared. While you are here, you are going to learn how to turn away from your sins.

As we see these afflictions happening, we know the judgment and the fierce anger of the Lord are coming. Our people are clueless about what is about to happen to them; in America we are so comfortable that hard living means cancelling Netflix. It is our job to warn them, and they have to be willing to listen and be gathered before the decree brings forth.

precepts.label: Amos 5:15
precepts.why:
Amos shows an Israel that hates the righteous: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.” They tread upon the poor, build houses of hewn stone and plant pleasant vineyards, “but ye shall not dwell in them”. Don't be comfortable, family; that is what Amos is saying. A few verses on he tells them what to hate instead: “Hate the evil, and love the good”.

David said, I love thy commandments, and I hate every false way. We hate anything outside of keeping God's commandments: sin. We are supposed to hate sin, hate the fact that there is sin in our community, and do something about it by keeping God's law. We are not supposed to tolerate evil amongst our people.

Love the good is love God's commandments. That is your purpose, it is what increases your faith, and it is why you are called to magnify God's law.

“And establish judgment in the gate”: establish judgment in yourself, your household, your nation and your communities. Then “it may be that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.” You receive mercy when you hate the evil and love the good. That is the turn Amos calls for: stop hating the one who rebukes in the gate, and hate the sin instead. We separate ourselves from evil, the ways of our oppressor, and we strive for perfection.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:1
precepts.why:
Matthew writes “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”, and Isaiah had already written it: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.”

Matthew says “Galilee of the Gentiles”; Isaiah says “Galilee of the nations.” So the nations also means the Gentiles. Same land, same people, same word.

What we read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament. When the apostles and prophets spoke, they had to substantiate their points from what we call the Old Testament today. Whatever they said, they had to be able to justify it with that text. Matthew is not saying something new; he is showing the prophecy fulfilled.

This is the foundation for Acts 10. By the biblical text the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles, like strangers, like heathens. The New Testament shows Paul going out to find them scattered among the nations and bring them back to God, because the prophecy sent from the Old Testament was that the job was to raise up the 12 tribes of Israel again. The Gentiles of Galilee are Israelites that were scattered and cut off, and God is gathering them back.

precepts.label: James 5:16
precepts.why:
The Pharisees asked, “Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” Why is Christ sitting and communicating with ungodly people? To bring them to repentance. That was the whole purpose: “I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” So if you think you're right, then he's not here for you. The first step of changing is to acknowledge that we have issues.

James shows that first step: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.” You have to confess your faults so that we can pray for you and you can be healed. There is no healing without confession.

You can't cherry-pick what you want out of the Bible and expect to be received of God and Christ. Christ said, I came for the sick, those that need healing. But the sick have to own that they are sick. Many people are right in their own eyes; we don't want to see ourselves in a negative light and we act like the parts of us that aren't right will be all right with God. We will fall short of the kingdom if we keep that mindset of not changing.

So confession is where the physician's work begins. The one who acknowledges his faults can be prayed for and healed; the one who hides them, looking the part with fringes and a beard, stays sick.

precepts.label: Psalms 107:20
precepts.why:
Christ said, “They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” He came for the sick, those that need healing. So what do we use to heal ourselves? The psalm answers: “He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.”

He sent his word down to heal them. Write that down. The word of God is the medicine the physician brings.

So, men, do you know what the will of God is? Then you are ahead of the whole world, because people out here are crazy. People think you can still eat pork, or whatever you do, vote for Trump, whatever people are doing in this world. But you know his word, and his word is what is going to heal.

That is how the sinners at Christ's table were to be made whole: not by sacrifices, but by receiving the word he sent and letting it deliver them from their destructions. We all come in here sick, and we need to get cured.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:69
precepts.why:
Ezra speaks of God “being judge”, and of those “that are cured with his word.” Cured with his word: that is why Christ said, I didn't come for the righteous, I came for the sick, and I am going to give them my word so they can be healed and cured.

Read on and Ezra shows what would happen if God did not forgive those who are cured by his word and put out the multitude of contentions: “There should be very few left peradventure in an innumerable multitude.” Out of all the multitude, hardly any would be left.

So the word of God will cure you; it will heal you. When James says, confess your faults one to another and pray for one another that you may be healed, we have to apply the word of God. That is the cure the physician gives to sinners.

And that is the meaning of “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” We used to give sacrifices to absolve us for the sins we committed, but that is not how it was supposed to be from the beginning. The Lord said, I want to see you change rather than keep on sacrificing. His mercy is for those who are cured with his word and actually change.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:3
precepts.why:
A critic was played mocking the Israelites, quoting “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest” as if Christ said it to everybody: come unto me all ye, not you that accept that I'm black. That is what Edom is doing now, hiring black people, dumb Africans, to use Zionist talking points against the truth. We didn't say it; a black man said it. So here is the precept he does not know.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” Rest from what? From thy sorrow. From thy fear. From the hard bondage: that's slavery. Wherein thou wast made to serve. The man on the screen don't know what the hell he's talking about.

The rest Christ promises the labouring and heavy laden is rest from the sorrow, the fear and the hard bondage of Israel's captivity. The ones heavy laden are the people who were made to serve. That is who “come unto me” is addressed to.

Isaiah opens the chapter by saying who gets that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel.” We are messed up as a people, not in our right minds yet, but because of the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob he will yet choose us. That's mercy, and we need that mercy.

precepts.label: Luke 22:31-34
precepts.why:
God said, “Behold, I send my messenger before thy face”: John, sent to teach the people and get them right to prepare for Christ. That is the job of the prophet, the apostle and every teacher: to show you. Then Christ called Simon and Andrew, James and John, from their nets. These men came in to get right, and do you think that walking with him he was not showing them all their errors? Luke shows him doing it with Peter.

“And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you get right, then go strengthen your brethren. Christ is showing Peter he still has things to work on. You want to walk with me? I'm going to show you what your problems are.

Peter answered, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.” And Christ said, “I tell thee, Peter”, didn't you just hear what I said to you? “the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.” Peter, you ain't there yet. Your mind ain't right yet. Get converted first.

Peter did become the head of the church afterwards, but first there were things he had to reconcile within himself. God opens his book and we behold ourselves in it; he sends prophets to show us how to get right. The worst thing to do is deny it. It don't feel good when you're going through it, but it's good for you. Medicine hurts sometimes, but if you are sincere you take your medicine and you get better. If you don't, you become an example of what not to do.

And those who teach must turn it on themselves too: don't weaponize the scriptures to correct everybody else while you can't see your own flaws, or hold brothers to a perfection you yourself are far from.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
Christ says “that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.” What is the will of God? David defines it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

God defines his will as his law. His will for us is that we keep the commandments. So the servant in Luke 12:47 who knew his Lord's will is the one who knew the laws of God and prepared not himself.

Preparing yourself means measuring yourself against the Bible, men and women alike. The Bible is the measuring barometer we look at to see whether we are pairing ourselves off right with God. If we are really honest and examine ourselves, in many cases we are not: if Christ came back right now, many of us are not ready. It comes down to opening the book, reading it for what it says, and doing what it says.

Much was given to us. We have the keys to the kingdom of heaven: the will of God, which people live a whole life and never understand, thinking a Hail Mary or gospel songs will have them holding hands with Jesus in the kingdom, not knowing that believing is an action word. Because we know his will, much more will be required of us, and as you move up in rank the road gets narrower until you have to walk blameless. We tell the people to do this and not do that, so we had better live it, or we will be beaten with many stripes.

thread.text: And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

classes.title: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:16-17
precepts.why:
Christ “took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it”, and said, “This is my body which is given for you”. Paul shows what that breaking of bread is: “The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?”

“For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.” We are all partakers of that manna. Christ is the true manna, the bread from heaven, and we feed upon Christ through his words.

So when we break bread together we are not only eating a piece of bread. We are showing that we are one body, all of us feeding on the same bread, which is Christ and the word of God. That is the fuller sense of “this do in remembrance of me.”

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 11:23-25
precepts.why:
We do this every Sabbath, and here is another reason to take it seriously. Paul received it of the Lord: “the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.” Then “This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.”

The broken bread, the remembrance, the body, the sacrifice: he is the true manna. You break bread every time we come together, but are you eating the bread that is abundant for us? Breaking bread once a week and thinking that is all right is not enough. The breaking of bread is also symbolic of that manna and the commitment we have to consume God's word every day, day and night.

Revelation 2:17 promises it: “To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna”. The body is dying; you are born and on a path to death. The flesh fights, the mind forgets, and the soul is weighed down by this tabernacle, so the inward man has to be renewed and kept alive by the word daily. The manna showed it, the prophets lived it, David meditated on it, Paul explained it, and Christ revealed himself to be that true bread from heaven. “It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.”

In the wilderness Israel sacrificed daily, twice daily. Psalm 51: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it”, but “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” If we really considered our ways, our thoughts and our behaviors, we would understand why we need to seek him daily and continually to forgive our sins; feeding yourself so sparingly, you won't understand this.

precepts.label: Hosea 4:17
precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” These Samaritans were Israelites who still lived there. Samaria is north of Jerusalem, as the map shows, and the Jews of Jerusalem stopped dealing with our people located in Samaria.

Why did that happen? A brother answered from Hosea: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why she said it. The scripture said Ephraim was joined to idols, and the word was to let him alone.

So the separation between the Jews and the Samaritans was not just a grudge; it grew out of the judgment on the northern kingdom for its idolatry. Judah took that word and left Ephraim alone. Yet here Christ, of Judah, sits at Jacob's well and asks a woman of Samaria to give him drink.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:6-11
precepts.why:
Hosea shows why Ephraim was let alone. “Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” He would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, because they fully went into idolatry. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen”, as can be read in 2 Kings 19.

“Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” That was the message to the northern kingdom because of his anger at their idolatry: you will not be my people, and I will not be your God. That is why the woman said the Jews have no dealings with us.

But then it comes back: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again.

All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to change and repent. If there were no endgame where we come out of this, there would be no incentive. But God said if you turn back to me, in the place where it was said you are not my people, there you will be called the sons of God.

precepts.label: Isaiah 7:8
precepts.why:
Before Hosea recorded the Lord casting off the house of Israel, Isaiah had already prophesied it: “For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.”

They already knew. God already told them that within sixty-five years Ephraim, the northern kingdom, would be broken and destroyed, and that is what Hosea 1 is recording: Lo–ruhamah, no more mercy on the house of Israel, and Lo–ammi, ye are not my people.

So when the woman of Samaria says the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans, she is standing at the end of that prophecy. Ephraim was broken “that it be not a people”, cut off for idolatry. And that is exactly why it matters that Christ, a Jew, is speaking to her at Jacob's well: the people who were broken off are about to be offered the living water.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:26
precepts.why:
Christ told her, “If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” What is the living water? A brother answered from Ephesians: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”.

You are cleansed by the washing of water by the word, so the living water is the word of God. What Christ would have given her was understanding: the understanding that the tribes were going to be gathered back together again.

She said, “Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well”? That shows she understood she was part of the twelve tribes of Israel; she just knew the Jews had no dealings with them. And Christ answered, “Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst”. The water, the understanding he was going to give her, would bring about the kingdom and salvation for them, because they had been disconnected from it for so long.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:23-29
precepts.why:
The water Christ gives is “a well of water springing up into everlasting life”, and Paul shows what that understanding is. He is a minister of the gospel “which was preached to every creature which is under heaven”, to fulfil the word of God: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints”.

It was hid for ages that the northern kingdom had a part to play in this, to repent and come back. The ones who did understand were the learned men who studied, many of them the Pharisees, which is why they said, will he go to the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach them? They read Isaiah, Ezekiel and Deuteronomy. The masses didn't have the scriptures; the learned men had the parchment. But now he gave it to the apostles to teach.

“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory”. The riches of this mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom has an opportunity of repentance: he is gathering back the Gentiles. The secret hid for ages is being revealed to the whole world; it is no longer gatekept. The apostles would go throughout the earth and teach the people that you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, whatever byword was given to you: you are the children of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom”.

That is what is happening to us now. The understanding of this Bible and of who we are was hid for ages, but the Lord said in this hour the true worshippers are going to wake up.

precepts.label: Joshua 8:30-35
precepts.why:
The woman at the well said, “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. On the map, the mountains above the well are Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. Joshua 8 shows why she said it: “Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.” “And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.”

When we first came into the land, the first place we came into was what would be called Samaria, and the first altars were set up in Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. That is why, when the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there: this is the place where we worshipped initially. But God called his home Jerusalem; that is where he set up his temple.

Read on: “And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”. The blessings went up on the children of Israel, and the cursing was on Mount Ebal.

“There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.” When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude of the other nations among us, and they were conversant in the laws of God. They had to learn the laws. We taught them how to keep the Sabbath day: six days you do your work, and on the seventh no work, neither your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.

Then Christ answered her: “Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” There was a time coming, 70 AD, when Jerusalem would be toppled by the Romans, and neither the mountains of Samaria nor Jerusalem would matter, because he was destroying it. His purpose was to gather in one the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.label: John 5:30
precepts.why:
“Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me.” Who sent Jesus? Christ answers it himself: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

He did not come on his own errand. He was sent from his Father, and he sought only the Father's will. And that will was to gather the twelve tribes of Israel: other sheep he must bring in, that there might be one fold and one shepherd. The gathering began when Christ came and began to teach, and his death was the beginning of the twelve tribes being brought back together.

So when he says he goes “unto him that sent me”, he is going back to the Father whose will he came to do. What that will was, the prophets had already written, and Isaiah 11 shows it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:1-3
precepts.why:
The Old Testament shows who was sent and why. “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”: that Branch is Christ, as Zechariah 6 shows. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.”

Then: “and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears.” That is the same exact thing Christ said in John 5:30: “as I hear, I judge”, “I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” The Branch out of Jesse does not judge by himself; he does the will of the one who sent him.

So what did God send him to do? Keep reading in the same chapter, and verse 12 tells it: to set up an ensign, assemble the outcasts of Israel and gather the dispersed of Judah. When Christ spoke in the New Testament, he was reiterating what the Old Testament already said, and the text substantiates it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:10-12
precepts.why:
“And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” Who are the Gentiles here? The Jews in John 7 asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The answer is Israel, and it is proven by staying in the passage.

“the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The Gentiles that seek the root of Jesse are the outcasts of Israel, the remnant of his people.

That was God's will in sending his Son: to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. The Pharisees and chief priests were studied men. They understood this prophecy of the dispersed, which is why they asked whether he would go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles.

precepts.label: Proverbs 1:27-28
precepts.why:
“Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.” The Old Testament already spoke it: “When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you. Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me.”

They will not. The same words Christ spoke to the Pharisees and chief priests are written in Proverbs, against those who would not hear. When Christ, the apostles and the prophets spoke in the New Testament, their conversation was reiterating what the Old Testament was saying, and they could substantiate it with the text.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:64
precepts.why:
Isaiah 11 says “he shall set up an ensign for the nations”. Why for the nations? Because Israel was going to be scattered: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were going to be scattered in all these nations and live as Gentiles, serving other gods. So the ensign set up for the nations is set up to “assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The ones he gathers out of the nations are Israel.

That is what the Jews meant in John 7 when they asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles”? They knew the curse: Israel scattered from one end of the earth to the other.

precepts.label: Tobit 3:4
precepts.why:
Tobit shows the dispersed are Israel once again: “For they obeyed not thy commandments: wherefore thou hast delivered us for a spoil, and unto captivity, and unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.”

Israel disobeyed the commandments, and so was delivered for a spoil, into captivity, unto death, and made a proverb of reproach among all the nations where they were dispersed. The Pharisees understood Tobit and the dispersed, just as they understood Isaiah 11. That is why they said of Christ, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” They knew who the dispersed were.

precepts.label: Tobit 13:5
precepts.why:
“And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he hath scattered us.” Again it uses the word nations, explaining that it was Israel being scattered among them.

The scourge is for our iniquities, but mercy comes again, and the promise is the gathering out of all nations. That is the same gathering Isaiah 11 speaks of, and the same work Christ was sent to begin: bringing the dispersed out from among the Gentiles, where they had been scattered.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 36:19
precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the same: “And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.”

They're dispersed. Israel was scattered among the heathen and dispersed through the countries, judged according to their own ways and doings. The Pharisees and chief priests understood Ezekiel 36 and the dispersed, along with Isaiah 11 and Tobit 3. So when they asked, “Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?”, they were speaking of scattered Israel living among the heathen.

precepts.label: Acts 21:21
precepts.why:
The New Testament shows the dispersed being taught: “And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.” There were Jews among the Gentiles, and Paul was going to them.

We know from the text that the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles. Coming back to the New Testament, it shows Paul going out to find the Jews scattered among these other nations, living like Gentiles, living like strangers, living like heathens, and bringing them back to God.

This was the prophecy sent from the Old Testament: the job was to raise up the twelve tribes of Israel again. What the Jews in John 7 asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles”?, is exactly what was done.

precepts.label: Psalms 95:1-7
precepts.why:
Everything Christ and the apostles spoke was already spoken in what we call the Old Testament, and they used it to substantiate their points. So when Christ says of his other sheep, “they shall hear my voice”, the psalm already said it.

“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” The rock of our salvation is Christ. “For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the deep places of the earth”; “The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker.”

“For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice.” We are the sheep of his hand, and the condition is the same: if you will hear his voice. That is exactly what Christ said in John 10: “them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice.”

For all of us there was a time that we heard this voice. We heard the word of God, and it brought us to repentance, to change. Something innate in us made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life. That is how the sheep of his pasture are known.

precepts.label: Micah 2:12
precepts.why:
Christ said, “there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.” The fold he was speaking in was the Jews in Jerusalem, primarily Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The other sheep, not of that fold, were the rest of Israel, and he would gather the two nations, the southern and northern kingdoms, together under one shepherd, Jesus Christ.

Micah prophesied that one fold: “I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men.”

“all of thee” means all twelve tribes. That is the same thing Christ was saying: I have sheep that are not of this fold; them also I must bring, that there may be one fold and one shepherd. The prophecy was that all twelve tribes were going to be brought back together.

The beginning of it coming to fruition was when Christ came and began to teach, and his dying was the beginning of the twelve tribes being gathered back together. That is what his death was about: he was sent by his Father to gather the flock of Jacob into one fold.

precepts.label: 1 John 2:6
precepts.why:
Christ says, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” This goes into the bread of life: everything that happened with the manna was always symbolic of Christ, a shadow foreshadowing him. And the first thing he calls himself is the way.

John tells us what it means for Christ to be the way: “He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.” We have to walk as he walked.

Christ is not a way you only talk about or feel; he is a path you walk. Whoever says he abides in Christ has to walk the same way Christ walked, in the same commandments, day by day. That is what it means to feed on him as the bread from heaven: to take in his word every day and live the way he lived.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:142
precepts.why:
Christ says he is also “the truth.” The psalm says what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

God's law is the truth, and Christ is the embodiment of all these things. He fulfilled, and will fulfil, all the prophecies: he came in the volume of the book, as it was written of him.

So when Christ says, I am the truth, he is saying he is the law of God walking in the flesh. Everything from beginning to end has Christ in it, which is why the Old Testament established everything else, and why we need here a little and there a little to unlock the scriptures. To come to the Father by Christ is to come by the truth, his everlasting righteousness and his law.

precepts.label: John 4:14
precepts.why:
Christ says he is “the life.” He tells the woman at the well: “But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.”

He is that sustenance again. Just as he said, “he that believeth on me shall never thirst”, he is the water as well as the bread. Remember in 1 Corinthians 10 it says they all ate the same spiritual meat and all drank of that same spiritual drink, from the spiritual rock in the wilderness.

The water out of the rock physically happened so that they could live, and so that we could have its meaning today. The water Christ gives becomes a well inside you, springing up into everlasting life. That is why he is the life.

precepts.label: 1 John 5:10-12
precepts.why:
“He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.” Christians stop and say this record is exclusively the New Testament. No. The record that God gave of his Son is the whole Bible, starting in the Old Testament.

At the time these letters were written, maybe they had the gospels at best, but a lot of the New Testament was not there. So where do you find the record God gave? In the Old Testament: the manna, the cloud, the rock, the water that came out of it so that they could live. It physically happened so that we could have that today.

“And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.” That is the daily bread, the daily nourishment. “He that hath the Son hath life”: that is the bread, the sustenance from heaven, the Holy Spirit. “and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.”

So it is not just, oh, I accept Christ, and that's all. It is everything we have read up to this point and everything in the Bible in its totality. That is the life Christ means when he says, I am the life.

precepts.label: John 10:9
precepts.why:
The last part of John 14:6 is “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” By Christ we know the Father. He says it another way: “I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.”

He is that door. You want to get to the Most High? You have to enter in through Christ, and whoever enters by him shall be saved.

“and shall go in and out, and find pasture.” He shall go in and out and find pasture, and find that rest. The door is the only way in to the Father, and on the other side of it is the pasture and the rest the sheep are fed with. That is how the bread from heaven feeds a dying man: by coming through Christ.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 2:5
precepts.why:
Christ says, “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” Paul says the same: “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

He is the life. There is one God and one mediator between God and men, and that mediator is the man Christ Jesus. Nobody else stands between us and the Father: not a priest, not a saint, not anybody else.

That is why he is the way, the truth and the life, the manna from heaven and the door. The flesh is dying, the mind forgets, and the inward man has to be renewed daily by the word. The only way that renewing reaches us from the Father is through the one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.

precepts.label: Acts 4:31
precepts.why:
On the day of Pentecost “suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting”, and “they were all filled with the Holy Ghost.” That Holy Ghost was the mighty wind that filled them.

Acts 4 shows the same thing again: “And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.” The place shook, the Holy Ghost filled them, and the result was boldness.

When the apostles spoke and the Holy Ghost filled them, they were bold in what they said, because they knew what they were saying was sent of God, and they could prove it from the scriptures. That is the spirit that came on them at Pentecost: not a show, but a boldness to speak the word of God, grounded in knowing it.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 48:12-13
precepts.why:
The Holy Ghost came at Pentecost as a rushing mighty wind. Sirach tells of another man covered by the wind: “Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: whilst he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.”

Look what it says next: “No word could overcome him; and after his death his body prophesied.” While the spirit of God was on him, no word could overcome him.

Men, study. When you are out in the street, there should be no word that can confound you. We should not be hearing men teaching who cannot explain basic scriptures. We are going up against, for the most part, Christians, and they don't know the Bible. We should know who we are and how to explain it: Galatians 3, Ephesians 2:11-16. This is very elementary.

When the spirit of God is on you, no word should be able to overcome you. That is what filled the apostles at Pentecost, and that is what should fill the men who go out to teach today.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:9-10
precepts.why:
At Pentecost the Holy Ghost came as a wind. Ezekiel was told to prophesy to the wind: “Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord God; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.” That is the word of God coming upon them.

“So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.”

That is what was happening in Acts. They taught, and the people came in and gathered: devout men out of every nation under heaven, the scattered of Israel, hearing the word in their own tongues and standing up again.

All of you are here because the word of God was breathed on you, and it wasn't because the people teaching were shaky. So for you men out there teaching: study to shew thyself approved. The breath that raises the slain into an exceeding great army comes through a word that is taught with power.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:3
precepts.why:
At Pentecost they “began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.” Other tongues means other languages. The psalm already said it: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.”

There is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard. The devout men dwelling at Jerusalem came “out of every nation under heaven”, because according to Deuteronomy 28 we were going to be scattered into all nations. Every man heard the apostles speak in his own language, and they marvelled, “are not all these which speak Galileans?” That is because we were scattered among the heathen and learned their languages.

So God made sure the word reached every one of them in the tongue wherein they were born. In every language the scattered people of Israel had taken on, their voice was heard, and the gathering of the twelve tribes began.
