thread.label: James 1:5
thread.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 51:12-21
precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God.” How do we ask of God? Do you think wisdom just floats down from heaven? No. You have to study; you have to open the book. And how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you. As you grow in understanding you realize, like Paul, an expert in the law, that you had not known sin but by the law: I didn't know this was covetousness. Now you know what you have to fix in you.

Ecclesiasticus shows the man who asked: “When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.” He seeks wisdom to the end because wisdom will direct your path. “For thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee”: I will thank you because you will deliver me from that evil path.

“I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness.” I redirected what I was doing and directed my soul to wisdom, because wisdom in its pureness will direct my path and save me. You want to be tethered to wisdom because with wisdom you avoid the punishment. That's what we all want: to get ourselves right, to be a better servant, a better husband, a better father. Teach me, God. Well, somebody has to teach you.

“I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.” As you seek her, you start realizing all the issues you have, and the severity of what God is talking about: eternal damnation, some learning it after death by pain. I can't get past this porn, I can't get past lying. At first it sounds good: I put on fringes, we keep the feast days, we turn up. But now I'm learning, damn, I'm a hateful ass brother, I'm a murmurer, I'm a backbiter. My heart is troubled.

Then: “Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.” You come to the house of learning, and somebody is going to teach you how to direct yourself. So now they're teaching you, and now you're mad? Do we understand what we signed up for? You said you wanted wisdom; here it is. No, you don't really want wisdom. You want church.

precepts.label: Psalms 139:23-24
precepts.why:
If any man lack wisdom, let him ask of God: you pray, you ask of God, then you go to a house of learning and you learn. And what are you asking for? “Search me, O God, and know my heart”: know what I think, how I process your information. “try me, and know my thoughts”: I'm asking God to measure me against his word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there's any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That's what we are all asking God to do: show us. So when you ask God for wisdom and he starts showing you your errors, that is the prayer being answered.

That's why James says, “My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations.” You count it joy because you asked, show me all my wicked ways so I can fix them. “But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask God to show you, the scripture comes correcting you, and now you're wavering. What are you doing when you waver? Trying to dodge correction.

So when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the sin a person commits so much as what they do afterwards that shows who they are, because none of us is right. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Big talk, and as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses. Blessed is the man that endures it: just listen, learn, and live.

thread.label: James 1:6-8
thread.text: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 4:26
precepts.why:
“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” You ask God in faith to show you about you so you can fix you, knowing he will direct you on the right path. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” Now you have asked God to show you, the scripture comes to you correcting, and you are wavering. What are you trying to do when you waver? You are trying to dodge correction.

Sirach says it: “Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river.” Here is the river, flowing. You are trying to reroute it away from you, trying to make it go another direction. You are dodging correction and making it seem like something it is not.

That is the double minded man, “unstable in all his ways”: always tossed around, forever moving, never straight, never steady, never going head on. With God “is no variableness”; with man there is variableness: jumping all over the place, can’t take it, making excuses, always responding, always having something to say, never listening. Some start answering before you can even finish the sentence; they are not listening to understand, they are listening to respond. A man of wisdom listens from a neutral position, takes in all the information, then discerns whether it fits him.

You said you wanted wisdom. Here it is. So don’t be ashamed to confess your sins, and don’t force the course of the river.

precepts.label: Amos 5:24
precepts.why:
The one who wavers is trying to dodge correction, to force the course of the river. Amos shows the river as it should flow: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”

That is a river. Let judgment run down as waters. Let it run. Don’t waver and try to get around it; don’t try to force the course to divert it. Let judgment come down, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

You asked God to show you your errors, and he is showing you. “For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” If you keep rerouting the judgment away from yourself, you will not receive the wisdom you asked for. Let it run down on you, accept it, and fix what it shows you.

precepts.label: Micah 7:9
precepts.why:
“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” What is that person saying? He is taking accountability: I will bear the judgment of God, because I have sinned. “until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

Don’t try to get around the cause. Don’t try to deviate from the judgment. Don’t make excuses. Stop wavering. You asked God to show you, he has shown you where you are wrong, and now you are trying to bypass it: maybe I would be better if you brothers called me and checked in on me; it’s your fault. Do you think this is Disney and this is a ride? You can ride that pony by yourself.

Why will he bring me forth to the light? Because I don’t dodge what I asked for. I asked God to show me my secret faults and my errors because I want to get better, and now that he is showing me, this is not the time to start dodging. We all fall short.

How do you endure in the truth? Listen, learn and live. There is no special recipe: when it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. As soon as the medicine comes, people start running. The infraction does not tell who a person is so much as what they do afterwards: do they take their medicine, the scriptures? If they can’t, they lose respect. All the big words mean nothing if, as soon as correction comes, they ghost and make excuses because of pride and ego.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:1
precepts.why:
When people come into this faith, the challenge is dealing with the spiritual man as opposed to the carnal man. They pray for wisdom, for discernment, to grow in the truth, and then they will not listen to the men appointed before them, because the carnal man or carnal woman does not see things spiritually. Ezra shows the spirit behind it: “Thus saith the Lord, I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them my commandments by menservants the prophets; whom they would not hear, but despised my counsels.”

God gave his commandments by the prophets to teach the people, and they would not hear the prophets. But whose counsels did they despise? “my counsels”: God’s. The prophets open the scriptures and show you thus saith the Lord to help you overcome what you are dealing with, and when you resist, it is the counsel God truly gave you that you despise. It came through men, but God inspired it.

So whoever brings correction your way, men or women, it is for your benefit, and they are being inspired by the Lord to direct you according to the path you should walk. Be humble, be quiet and listen. They are coming out of the scriptures and showing your error. Learn; this is how we grow. The carnal man will cause you to resist the direction God wants you to grow in, and that is the wavering, double minded man who shall not receive any thing of the Lord.

All scripture is given by inspiration of God for reproof, correction and instruction in righteousness. It is not a book to tote your ego so you feel good. If the Lord showed us who we are, we would be ashamed; it is only the mercy of Christ and his promise that we are here. For us to change, somebody has to tell us what we were doing wrong, and when they do, don’t get mad.

precepts.label: James 4:7-8
precepts.why:
“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God.” You want to blame somebody: Lord, it ain’t me, you put that big booty woman in front of me. The Lord says stop, bro. I put the nine millimeter in front of you, but you didn’t shoot yourself; I put the knife in your hand; I put the crack pipe in the room, but you didn’t smoke it. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed is when something appeals to you and you give in; you entertain it. That is on you; that is your choice. God is just showing you what your vice is, and now that is what you are fighting.

When you are tempted, you are supposed to resist. James tells how: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” Submit yourself to God: take the counsel. How do you resist the devil? By first submitting yourself to God.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” How are you going to draw nigh to God? Somebody is going to teach you and you are going to learn; you go to the house of learning. That is what you are doing now. And God will draw nigh to you and give you a way to escape. “Blessed is the man that endureth temptation.” How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? You don’t know you can bench 315 until it is on the rack. You are asking for muscles; you have to lift.

“Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” We just read that in chapter one: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” Now that you hear the correction about how to get right with God, you have excuses. You see the sin in front of you and turn away, like seeing a booger in your nose in the mirror and turning your head; the booger is still there. “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls. But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only.” The glass is the Bible; you see yourself in it and walk away and forget. You can close the book; you are still a sinner. Submit, resist, draw nigh, and cleanse your hands.

thread.text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Mark 7:21
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Lust has nothing to do with love, and love has nothing to do with lust; a lot of us get those two confused. What is a man’s own lust? Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.”

Read on: “Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” Adultery and fornication are sins we battle every day. The spirit of murder you see in this world, and our people fight that demon every day. Covetousness we fight every day, because we lust and covet after these things. Deceit is a demon we fight every day.

These come from within. So the battle is not really from the outside; the thing we lust after is within us, and the battlefield is the mind. A brother can be quiet here but fighting major demons; a sister can be quiet but fighting demons. Quiet does not mean humble. Some are bound with their sin.

And this world feeds it. Everything here is a work of sin. They sell sex everywhere; you think you are watching a movie or a karate flick, and they put that nasty thing in there, and down the line you see how people turn to watching porn. The devil is always there, pushing sin. That is why we have to understand this walk and overcome it: every man is drawn away of his own lust, the evil that comes from within his heart.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 32:26
precepts.why:
“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous. The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect; an animal could not be spotted. And James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” But we all fall short.

So who is James writing to? “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

thread.label: James 1:25
thread.text: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:8
precepts.why:
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:10
precepts.why:
The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

thread.label: James 4:1
thread.text: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: James 3:15-16
precepts.why:
James 4:1 asks, “From whence come wars and fightings among you?” When you are told something you are doing wrong and something in you is adverse to correction, right is coming in and wrong is warring against it. Captains who have sat in counsel know the look: you tell somebody they don't listen, and they squint like they are confused and repeat back what you just said. It ain't their sight that went bad. It is the battle in the mind, manifesting in the face.

James shows where that confusion comes from: “For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness in it, and there should be no confusion in what is being said. If you were sincere, you would say, show me the lie, help me understand, maybe I am in error. Instead you are confused, because you are warring with what is right and don't want to accept it. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It is deceiving you, the same deceiving we read in chapter one.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you and why you can't move forward. You are a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer, it is being identified to you, and you cannot reason with yourself. You are struggling with yourself, and that is the war in your members.

precepts.label: James 4:10-11
precepts.why:
When a brother starts to correct you and you don't like it, what do brothers start doing? They get mad, they pull away, they hold a grudge, and then they start speaking evil of the ones who corrected them. James says: “Speak not evil one of another, brethren.”

What are you supposed to do instead? “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.” You are supposed to humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, because you know to do good, but you don't want to do it.

That is the war and the fighting of James 4:1, coming out of the lusts that war in your members. The correction comes in, the wrong inside wars against it, and instead of humbling yourself, the war turns outward into speaking evil of your brother. The one who humbles himself stops the war where it starts.

precepts.label: James 4:17
precepts.why:
“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” You know that what is being said is right, but you don't want to do it, because you are struggling. What is sin for you? Your sin is what you are struggling with. That is where the war is: you don't want to accept the prophet telling you.

That is all the people in the streets right now. You tell them what they are doing wrong and they are ready to kill you; they want to fight you for teaching the Bible. What's wrong with you? You hate to hear it because it convicts you. It is letting you know your life is in shambles, that you are evil, that you are the devil.

So the wars and fightings of James 4:1 come from knowing to do good and not doing it. The lust you are holding on to wars against the good you already know.

precepts.label: Job 9:20
precepts.why:
Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You are condemning yourself. The word of God, which comes from the teachers, is supposed to cleanse you, and the margin gives justify as cleanse, or clear self. So justifying yourself is deceiving yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear. Whatever the teachers have to say, the reproof and the instruction I'm receiving, I'm already clean.

When that happens, teachers, sometimes you have to let people suffer. Most people don't make the same mistake twice by accident; they choose, ignore the warnings, repeat the patterns, and expect someone else to absorb the consequences. Rescue delays the learning, and growth delayed by rescue is growth denied. David said it was good that he was afflicted. We can't carry everybody.

But teachers and instructors cannot weaponize the scriptures either, using them to correct everybody else and never our own lives. Then you are the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself, holding brothers to a higher accountability than you are willing to hold yourself, expecting perfection while you have hidden sins. The justified self is the one the mouth condemns, whether it is the one being corrected or the one correcting.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:165
precepts.why:
Peter says, “But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye.” We must begin to learn how to suffer for righteousness' sake, for the sake of Christ. And we are happy in it: that happiness is our peace. Happy are they that keep God's laws.

David shows where that peace comes from: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” Nothing shall offend them means offenses, and being afraid of tribulation, will not make you turn your back on Christ.

That is why Peter goes on, “and be not afraid of their terror”: the terror of being persecuted. Times are not going to get easy, for husband, wife, brother or sister, so we have to prepare ourselves for hard and trying times and not go railing for railing with one another. Our best tools are praying, fasting, studying and increasing our faith, and following the instructions laid forth.

The man or woman who loves God's law has a peace the world cannot shake. When the tribulation comes, the law they love keeps them from being offended, and they endure it happy, suffering for righteousness' sake.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:1
precepts.why:
Peter laid out the instructions for marriages, because hard times are coming. We see marriage troubles where a sister is upset because her husband's socks are on the floor and she calls him lazy; or a sister gives up the faith and wants to go back to the damn world and be a h-o-e to negro Tyrone instead of a wife to the husband the Lord gave her; or a brother wants to be a whoremonger instead of a man of his nation leading his people. There are more trying times coming, when you will be worried about surviving. How much more in a household where a man and woman are striving and going back and forth with each other?

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives.” Sisters, your tone, how you speak toward your husband, especially in hard times, means a lot. How you respect your lord, your king in your household, and how you carry yourself toward him shows the level of your faith. You sisters have to increase your faith and learn how to be correct with the man God gave you. And not just husband and wife: all you sisters must honor the men of your nation.

In hard times Satan attacks marriage. He did not attack the government Adam set up first; he attacked the foundation, the marriage, which shows how powerful marriage is. And he did it by going through the woman first, which is why you sisters have to build yourselves up.

The Bible says marriage is honorable and the bed undefiled: righteous marriage, husband and wife, as with Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Joseph and Mary, not man and man or woman and woman. Keeping that honorable is part of suffering for righteousness' sake and being happy in it.

thread.text: To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:9
precepts.why:
“To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame”. That is the business we are in: we have to overcome. With rank or without rank, a brother has to stay the same trooper. Don’t bail out now; it is time to stand up and face what we have to face.

What we have to overcome, Paul lays out: “Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” Your mother, your father, your aunt, if they are living an unrighteous life, will not inherit the kingdom. “Be not deceived”: not by Christianity, not by religion, not by the white man, not by the uncle or auntie telling you that you are in a cult. Satan can deceive you into leaving this life while you think you are still in the faith.

“Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind”. A lot of us are fighting the fornication spirit, the covetous spirit, the lustful demons. “Nor thieves”: some cannot stop stealing even in this truth, like the brother who borrowed the book and never brought it back. “Nor drunkards”: know your limit, because the drink spirit brings out whatever defilement is in your mind.

“And such were some of you.” That is the life we came from, so don’t think Satan won’t tempt you with these things now. And Galatians 6 warns: “if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every man prove his own work”. It is by the grace of God that you stand. When a brother or sister gets knocked out in this truth, your job is to fast and pray, never to applaud. Be your brother’s keeper; your sin may just not be revealed as quickly as his. That is how we overcome.

precepts.label: Isaiah 5:20
precepts.why:
“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” What are we coming out of? What this society promotes: adultery, the music, murder, sodomy, homosexuality, drunkenness, drug abuse, idolatry, wicked entertainment and corruption. All the things God hates, against his laws, statutes and commandments, and all of it deceives us. We must expose this evil so you can learn how to save your own soul. Look at what they call the YNs: our people smoking, toting guns, women with guns bigger than they are, little kids holding bullets. And then they call us a hate group when we are trying to stop the evil within our own community first.

Sin is deceitful, and America has blurred the line. Your president even asks, what do you have to lose? Choose the worst of both evils. Isaiah 5:20: “Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!” Woe is destruction unto them. That is how they blur the line between good and evil.

Who does that? Your pastor. Many a black church on every corner facilitates the continuance of your oppression. So you have to choose a side: righteousness, your heritage, your nation, keeping God’s commandments.

That is the second step: study, pray, apply, see yourself in the scriptures, and then show your faith by separating yourself from evil. Our purpose is Acts 26:18: “To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God”. That is coming out of her.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 1:5
thread.text: Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me; that they may tell their children’s children:

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17-18
precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 1:5 God commands the prophet: “Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds”. Go and show the people. Ezekiel was given the same charge: “get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then God tells him why: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

So as a prophet and teacher, it is required that we tell you what you are doing wrong, because if we don’t, we are liable to have that blood on our hands. It is not that we even have a choice. You call yourself a prophet, a teacher: your job is to go correct the people and help the brother.

That is why showing the people their sinful deeds is not hatred. Sometimes you have to show someone their shame, and that is God loving them too, because he could leave them right there to die and find out after death. It is our job to warn our people, to hopefully bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and they cannot want correction for others while refusing it for themselves.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
If you see a brother that is in error and you don’t correct him, what does the scripture say you are? “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”

If you see a brother in error and do not rebuke him, you hate your brother in your heart. Leaving sin upon him is not love; rebuking him in any wise is. So we have no choice but to tell our people what they are doing wrong, or we hate our brother in our heart.

That is the love behind 2 Esdras 1:5, “shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me”. Showing the people their sins is how you keep from hating them. And it goes both ways: when a brother comes to you and says this is wrong, hear it and learn, because you do not want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

thread.text: For as the husbandman soweth much seed upon the ground, and planteth many trees, and yet the thing that is sown good in his season cometh not up, neither doth all that is planted take root: even so is it of them that are

classes.title: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
Ezra says the husbandman's seed perishes “if it come not up, and receive not thy rain in due season; or if there come too much rain, and corrupt it”. The husbandman is the Most High, the seed is the word he sows in us, and the rain is wisdom. Anyone who has planted knows that if too much rain falls on a seed, it does not grow. How can too much rain corrupt a man? Paul shows it: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.”

A novice is somebody new in this truth, a beginner. Some brothers come in and catch on real quick. Why would a novice get lifted up with pride? Because he got too much rain, too much wisdom, and he cannot handle it. He starts getting high-minded, and then he falls into the condemnation of the devil: Satan destroys the seed that is in him. That is what it means when the scripture says too much rain can corrupt the seed. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

That is why the heavy teaching is eased off at times. You may love it when the class goes deep, but too much of that wisdom too fast can corrupt you. The deacons have been learning in this truth for over twenty years. When you see them go into certain things, it comes from years of being watered; nobody woke up one day able to break down the scriptures.

So the Most High gives the rain in its season, moderately, as Joel says, “the former rain moderately”, raising the waters little by little, from the ankles to the knees, so that we can handle it. The seed that receives its rain in due season takes root and bears fruit; the novice who is lifted up with pride perishes like the corrupted seed.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 14:13
thread.text: Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption,

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:9
precepts.why:
“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. Your body is a house; that is the house you live in. Set your life in order, brother, with God's laws, statutes and commandments, and then you can reprove and teach your people. And the Most High has set men over us to do that very work.

“And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.” Our leadership is wise, brothers and sisters; the Lord set them over us for a reason. They teach the people knowledge: how to overcome, how to lead ourselves in the way of righteousness.

Set in order many proverbs: that is what we do when we go over precepts. There are a lot of proverbs we read and don't understand, and leadership puts the puzzle together and sets them in order so you can understand the things of old. “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright”. They search out what the people need and what they are going through. Sometimes they step on toes, just to wake you up or break the chain you have been fighting with.

So God did not leave us without help. When we go off, he set up brothers and sisters to guide us back home. You can never say God did not send help; the one who ignores it is caught up in stupidity.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra to “comfort such of them as be in trouble”, and that comfort comes out of the scriptures: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That which was written was upright, and we have to understand it and follow it. That's the pattern.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. Don't let Satan take it away from you, and don't give it up for Babylon's money; Babylon will destroy your soul. Set your house in order, revive your own soul first, and then revive your people.

thread.label: 2 Esdras 16:76
thread.text: And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.

classes.title: Pattern

precepts.label: Psalms 94:16
precepts.why:
The Lord God says, “let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” And: “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes.” Brothers give up their position because of the affliction, the little tribulation, or because of their bills, two hundred-some thousand dollars of debt. How could you be that stupid, that ignorant? We all have bills. That is all you have. Their sin is wearing them down so much, and they are so covered with it that they cannot see the brotherhood right in front of them.

David asks the question every one of us has to answer: “Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” You have to stand up.

The evildoers are where we are today. Taking a man out of his country and bringing him back to America: the same America that pushes democracy, when democracy put him there, kidnaps him and charges him with unjust judgment. Is that just, or wicked? If it is hard for you to see that America is evil, it is because you are evil yourself. Everything here is a work of iniquity; they push sin everywhere, even in a little karate flick.

Christ said, “I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world.” Have the word of God and the world will hate you, and your family will hate you. “I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.” He left us in the world because we have a path to go through: from Adam until now it has been good against evil, and our job is to stand for what is right. “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The stony ground “immediately receive it with gladness”, but has no root, and when affliction arises “immediately they are offended.” What have you given for this truth? Many would wish to sit in a class learning they are the children of Israel, and many will die today without that chance. While you are alive, you still have it. So who will rise up and stand? Do not let your sins weigh you down.

thread.label: Wisdom of Solomon 7:1-25
thread.text: I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth,

classes.title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.label: Hebrews 4:12-13
precepts.why:
Wisdom “is the breath of the power of God.” The power of God is the word of God, and the word of God is wisdom. They're all synonymous; they all mean the same thing. The word of God is this book, and the word of God is Christ. It is one pureness, one avenue, with no variableness in what it means. That is why the Christian church has destroyed the minds of a people, making them believe you can separate Christ from the commandments. He is the word. You can't believe on Christ and not keep the commandments, and you can't keep the commandments and not believe on Christ. It's an oxymoron. Yet the witchcraft called Christianity has separated them to the point that it has been said that if you keep the commandments, you're sinning. Your church made you dumb as hell.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Quick means alive. This word is alive; it's not like a textbook. It will affect you to the deepest part of your thought process. It cuts, until you feel sick to your stomach, an emptiness like hunger. If you have never felt that cut in class, examine yourself.

“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” If you are tethered to Christ, you have to be tethered to wisdom, and if you are tethered to Christ and to wisdom, you know BS when you hear it. You know the intention of the heart of a person when they speak. You hear the pity party you've heard a thousand times before. You tell a man, stop talking, and he keeps talking, explaining, digging the ditch deeper, thinking he's making sense and embarrassing himself. A spiritual man discerneth all things. We could be wrong, we're not 100% with everything, we're learning ourselves; but for the most part, tethered to wisdom, you understand false speech.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 36:18-19
precepts.why:
“The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.” Why is one meat better than another? Because you can taste it. You have a palate, and you can say, I like this one better than that one.

“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” The same way your palate can taste which meat is better, a heart of understanding can discern false speech. You listen to somebody and you know: this is BS. It happened recently, around Passover, talking to a brother: listening for a while, it didn't add up, it started to sound like murmuring. You would have been better off keeping quiet, but being that you want to talk, go ahead and embarrass yourself.

That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7 is describing. Wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits.” If those are the attributes of wisdom, you want to be tethered to wisdom, so you can discern and understand why people do the things they do: the defense mechanism, the gaslighting, the one in error trying to tug on your heart and make you feel guilty so you will chase him. That's not how this goes. He is supposed to wear down the footsteps.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7-14
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2; it was wisdom, so that we should know better. And what is pure? “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” It will enlighten your spiritual eye to see things clearly, to understand false speech, to know when you're going in the wrong direction. It's supposed to light your path.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.” It is sweet, but then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. That's all right, because the law of God converts the soul. It's only a problem when your soul isn't getting converted.

“Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.” The Lord does not ask us to keep the laws with nothing in return; he is a just and fair God. And converting doesn't just happen; you don't close your eyes and wake up different. It comes through trial, error and correction.

“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults”: things people don't know I'm dealing with. Sometimes a class comes out talking right about you. You said you wanted wisdom. And if it comes in English and you speak Spanish, don't worry: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” We'll translate it, even into sign language. If it's for you, you'll get it. But you need to be cleansed.

“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me.” This is a prayer we ask God for, and then he sends the prophets to tell you. So why are you upset? Don't ask for rain and get mad when it's muddy. You asked God to cleanse you; he has to show you what needs to be cleansed. The first key is listening. The greatest gift a young person can have is to listen: be neutral, hear what's being said, examine yourself whether it's true, and if it is, fix it. Stop lying to yourself.

“then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression. Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.” If you want your words and your thoughts to be acceptable, open this book, learn what the will of God is, and when the word comes to you, accept it for what it says.

precepts.label: Psalms 141:5
precepts.why:
Converting comes through trial, error and correction, and you're supposed to be happy about the correction. “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness”: when that person is telling you what you're doing wrong, it's a kindness that he does it. “and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil”: it's going to be a blessing.

“which shall not break my head.” It isn't going to kill you. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is not going to kill you. It's supposed to kill the old man in you, not you physically. And people don't want to hear that; they don't want to know the errors of their ways.

When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptations, for trials, for tribulation. People come in with rose-colored glasses, thinking everything's going to be perfect. No: it's going to start unmasking who you are, who I am, and what we have to fix to get right. It's sweet until you start dealing with who you really are. That is the wisdom that leadeth and directeth the wise, as Solomon says: God directs you away from evil and shows you how to avoid it, and his reproof is how he does it.

precepts.label: Matthew 6:33
precepts.why:
Solomon says “I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.” Sometimes your job, whatever you have, becomes more important, and then you wonder why you can’t grow. Our chief love is the word of God. Jobs and careers are just for us to get by in this captivity; they should not be the focal point of your life. That is Matthew 6:33: seek the kingdom first, and everything else shall be added unto thee. That’s what the Bible says.

“Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.” That does not mean you just pray, God, give me understanding so I can break down Revelation. You pray to God, and God will tell you to study to show thyself approved and rightly divide the word. You have to choose this, and make him first.

“All gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.” Why is wisdom better than gold and silver? Those things are corruptible: they can be stolen or destroyed, and when you sell them the money runs out quick. Wisdom never runs out, because with wisdom you get the understanding to make more and to do this and that.

“I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.” I choose wisdom above all things; I prefer the Lord above all things. If you want understanding, call upon God and he will give it, but we have to make him first. Wisdom is “a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God”, and seeking that first is the beginning of the transition from milk to meat.

precepts.label: Mark 4:18-19
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:23 says wisdom is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care.” Free from what care? Free from worry and stress, and above all free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them.

“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of the world, the riches and the lusts of other things deceive you. Life does not consist in the abundance of things; they deceive you and choke the word.

Wisdom is free of those cares. The man that has wisdom is not going to be subject to the riches of this world. God said beware of covetousness, and that is wisdom, so I am going to beware of it; I am not going to entertain that.

So it is in our best interest to be paired with wisdom, because wisdom has “all power, overseeing all things.” Tether yourself to wisdom and you can see clearly, the cares of this world cannot choke the word, and it will not become unfruitful in you.

precepts.label: Hebrews 4:10-12
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 says wisdom is “the breath of the power of God.” What is the power of God? Hebrews 4 answers.

“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” We fought that example of unbelief. If we believe, we are tethered with God and following wisdom. Wisdom is pure, steadfast and sure, and we enter into that rest.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful.” Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 just said wisdom is “quick”, and “having all power.” The same words. And it is “sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.”

The intents of the heart are where sin begins. So we want that pure influence, so that the intents of this mind are not led astray and what guides and directs us is the word of God. There should be something in all of us that says, I can’t do that, it is wrong to do that. If we turn aside from that, we are saying we are hypocrites and don’t really believe. God has chosen us, for whatever reason, to give us wisdom. The power of God is the word of God. It is wisdom.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Wisdom is “a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Influence means to mold you and direct you. If wisdom is flowing down from the Almighty and it is influencing you, you are connected, tethered, with God. Or something else can be influencing you, and that will not be wisdom; it will be covetousness, lust, whatever it might be. Psalms 19 shows what that pure influence is.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were once simple, but wisdom is now in us, making us wise. “The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.”

That pure influence is the statutes, the laws of God. The commandment is “pure”, and it enlightens the eyes so that we can see clearly.

And if our eyes are enlightened and the Lord has converted us, what are we now? We are new, something different. That is where Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 goes: “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 10:6
precepts.why:
Psalms 19 showed the law converting the soul, and once converted we are new. 1 Samuel 10:6 says the same thing: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

With the word of God you change into another man. That is what Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 means: “she maketh all things new.” Wisdom will make you new, so you can’t keep doing the same thing.

But if the word is dealing with you and you are still trying to live that old man, still letting that old man tell you what to do, still doing that same stuff, the Lord says, I am going to beat you with many stripes, because I gave you something and you weren’t listening. Much is given, much is required. And don’t think many stripes is a pow pow and that is it. Many in that day will say “Lord, Lord”, and he is going to say, I don’t know you.

precepts.label: Luke 6:45-49
precepts.why:
“A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.” What comes out of his mouth is what is in him.

“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” Why are you calling me Lord, Lord, and don’t do the things I tell you to do? “Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.” “But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell.”

The one built on Christ, which is the rock, is the one that is applying it. Applying it is the whole key. That is what strengthens the foundation and lets us endure when tribulations come. Wisdom teaches us that, and it is plain to understand. In that day men will say, Lord, Lord, did not I prophesy? Yes, but you still didn’t do what I told you to do. You were out on the street teaching, but you were a hypocrite; you weren’t living it.

Brothers sometimes come up wanting to understand the deep prophecies. Brother, let’s first help you get off of Pornhub. Why are you in Revelation trying to understand these archangels? You have to let that stuff go. You know prophecy, but you don’t know you yet. Learn you, so you are able to live it, and then instruct people wisely and teach them how to serve God.

precepts.label: James 1:27
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:26: “For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” Wisdom is unspotted. James 1:27 shows how a man keeps himself the same way.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.”

You keep yourself unspotted from the world by visiting the fatherless and the afflicted, all people afflicted in the mind. But you are too busy trying to bag the chick. She came out of the world, out of whatever she was doing, and instead of leading her to God you are trying to sleep with her.

If we want to know how to keep ourselves unspotted, we tether ourselves to God, because flowing down from him is wisdom. You come into this truth not knowing any better, wisdom flows down from God to you, you apply it, and you become new: “she maketh all things new.”

precepts.label: Sirach 4:10
precepts.why:
Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 says wisdom, “in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” Wisdom cannot dwell in a body that is subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness or hatred. Ecclesiasticus 4:10 shows the conversion of our minds in these last days: when we put our interests over the Lord’s, it distances us from him, and when we put the Lord’s interests over ours, it brings us closer to the heavenly Father.

“Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother.” That is the opposite of the mindset of a whoremonger, who asks, what can I do to this sister, how can I take advantage of this single mother? The son of the Most High asks, what can I do for this young man to build him up? That is why Bishop Nathanyel says it is easier to build up a young man, a child, than to fix a broken old man; the broken old man is the one looking to take advantage.

“So shalt thou be as the son of the most High.” If you go opposite of that, you cannot be the son of the Most High. If you are looking at this sister with lustful eyes, trying to figure out how to get in her pants or take advantage of her, you can’t be the son of the Most High, and wisdom cannot dwell in you.

That is the charge on the friend of God and the prophet: to go out and raise up God’s children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy. Much is given to you, and much is going to be required of you.

precepts.label: Psalms 143:5
precepts.why:
Solomon says “the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” To muse, in the Bible, means to think deeply, meditate, ponder, or murmur on something, especially God's word or works, often in self communion, prayer and praise: to consider closely, to study in silence.

David uses that very word: “I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.” Listen to the word David used. He would think on why life is the way it is, why we suffer the conditions we suffer. Even Esdras said, Lord, it was not in my mind to know the deep things; I just want to know why Israel is jacked up, why we are going through what we are going through.

All of our minds muse daily upon many things. Why did that person die? Why is my life like this? Where did I go wrong? Should I have married her? Should I have gone to that job interview? Why did I get drunk last night? Most of you can't sleep; you toss and turn every night, especially the man who goes to work every morning carrying the burden of his whole family, or the father up at night thinking about what could happen to his daughters.

This earthy tabernacle, this corruptible body we got from Adam, is what makes us overthink and overanalyze everything. David's musing shows the right place to take it: remember the days of old, and meditate on the works of God's hands, because that is where the answer to why we suffer is found.

precepts.label: Hebrews 11:25
precepts.why:
Sirach says “Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman”, and it begins with the eyes. Your eyes are directly correlated with your mind; they work in sync, and what you see makes your mind react a certain way. When you see something inappropriate online, not even porn, which is obvious, but something you know is not right, and you find yourself clicking and looking, you are not in control. You are down that rabbit hole looking for that feel good, because sin feels good. It is enjoyable.

That is why Moses is set before us in Hebrews: “Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. The pleasure of sin is only for a season, and you are going to pay the price for it. There is a price that is going to be paid.

That little season we deem as pleasure is only pleasure because your mind has convinced you it is, and that is because you have made an agreement with your eyes to keep looking. That is what got David caught up. He did not look away, and it brought all the other problems that came along with it.

So the best thing to do is turn away. Turning your head is proof you have control of your members; that is called self-control. If you cannot turn away, Christ is not the captain of that ship; Satan is driving. “For many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman”, deceived because they looked and did not turn away, when a simple motion of the head could have saved them a world of problems. Moses chose affliction with the people of God over the pleasure; that is the choice set before us.

precepts.label: Matthew 12:34
precepts.why:
Sirach names the senses the Most High gave man: “They received the use of the five operations of the Lord, and in the sixth place he imparted them understanding, and in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the cogitations thereof.” Cogitation is the act of thinking very carefully and deeply about a subject, or a carefully considered thought itself; meditation is a good word for it too, the capacity to think or reflect.

So the sixth is understanding and the seventh is speech, and speech is the interpretation of what your mind meditates on. That is why “out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.” What you meditate on is what comes out of your mouth.

Thinking and reflecting do not work unless they are funnelled through the word of God; that is how your mind has to work. If you are not moving right, the thought that comes out is going to be off, and so will the speech that interprets it.

The list goes on: “Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand. Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.” The tongue is the instrument we use to form our words. Counsel is a man weighing options and determining what should be done, but he must be a godly man who surrounds himself with godly people. A mind fed on porn and then making decisions will make a mistake, and a mouth speaking out of that heart will show it. These senses are given so we can understand good and evil, and they have to be exercised in the word.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:4
precepts.why:
“Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: but he that resisteth pleasures crowneth his life.” That is the resist: resist the pleasure of sin. It is also in Hebrews, where the saints are striving against sin and resisting it. You are resisting sin.

James said it just before: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” If your eye is single, what are you resisting? All your appetites and all the lust you have. If your eye is single, you are on that path: “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.”

The opposite is the double-minded man: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” You are looking at the Lord and you are looking at Pornhub; you are looking at the Lord and you are in the midst of sin. “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other”. When your eye is not single, you hate God, because something else has your attention and your draw.

A brother who would not resist shows where it goes. It started with handing his phone to a woman at work while another brother stood a few feet away, no fear at all, and it spiralled into porn, the strip club and fornication. His heart was full of darkness: “If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!”

That is why Peter says “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the fleshly lust comes from what you look at, “the lust of the eyes”. You are at war, brothers, and if you are not resisting you are losing, while Satan is in your head saying you got it under control. The one who resists the pleasure crowns his life.

precepts.label: Job 32:7-8
precepts.why:
Sirach says “The law shall be found perfect without lies”, and “A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” It is talking about the man that knows the law and travels. Some of you were in the military and traveled, and you don't know nothing. Some of you are old and traveled here and there, and you don't know nothing, only because you don't know the law. Travel and years do not make wisdom without God's laws.

That goes back to Job 32: days should speak, and the multitude of years should show wisdom, but there is a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties amounted to nothing, but they want to be over men. You have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. They feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you are not at that level yet. Spiritually you are not growing; you are still at an infant stage. We don't care if you are eighty years old: if you don't know God's laws, you are an infant, a toddler, according to the word of God.

The understanding does not come from the number of years but from the spirit God puts in a man. Military men who have been to Syria and Iraq don't know what they are looking at, because they are not studied to know what to look for. The man whose years and travels are joined to the law is the one that declares wisdom.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:12
precepts.why:
That is why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he was going to be over some men older than him in age.

It doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom as though it is going to outshine God's wisdom. God is going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body, and that is just what it is. Be glad that you are part of this mission, and play your role.

It fits what Sirach 34 says: “The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.” Wisdom is in the law and the faithful mouth, not in the gray hair. A young man who knows God's laws, keeps them and labors in them, teaching all them that seek learning, is not to be despised because of his youth; and an older man who never learned the law is still an infant, however many years he has.

thread.label: Sirach 34:10-11
thread.text: He that hath no experience knoweth little: but he that hath travelled is full of prudence.

classes.title: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.label: Luke 14:23
precepts.why:
“He that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things”. Travelling doing what? Teaching. And another word for teaching, when you are going out, starts with an L: labour. That is Luke 14:23, the servant sent out by his lord. You are labouring for the Lord, for our people to wake up.

Sirach says the same of himself: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” You travel the world and seek out people that want to learn. But first you have to keep the commandments, learn and study, and then go out and teach. Military men travel too; they have been to Syria and Iraq, but they cannot tell you about Dura Europos or the walls of Cyrus. They travel, but they have not studied to know what to look for.

Judith shows why the labour matters: “Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” The people are depending on us, so it is our job to study, get right, and travel to share the word with our people. Later somebody comes behind you, and you share your experience and teach them. That is part of how you go from milk to meat.

The labour brings experience you cannot get staying home. In Cuba the police came with nightsticks and a paddy wagon; teaching without a license there could bring two years in jail with no trial, and the police chief said this teaching would cause a revolution. Having gone through that, the brethren learned there is a different way to approach it, not to stop teaching there. That is why it is good to get around learned men who have travelled: they understand more than they can express in one conversation.

And the one who labours for the Lord is kept by him: “I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.” “Whoso feareth the Lord shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.” If you are sincere in this truth and really keeping his commandments, that spirit will come on you and you will not fear. They said nobody could go up into Laventille in Trinidad because of the gangs; the brethren went up there to teach, and it put a spirit on those men, and now they go up there.

precepts.label: Psalms 66:18
precepts.why:
“But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should generally be spent around godly people. We have to go out in the world and work, but outside of that, the bulk of your time is with godly men, and if the brothers around you don't have understanding, be around people with more understanding than you so you can level up. How will you know he keeps the commandments? You have to be exercised to discern between good and evil. If you are keeping the commandments, you'll be around godly men, because every beast consorteth with its own kind.

He is one whose mind is according to thy mind, “and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he's going to correct you. So how is your mind? It has to be godly. When it says “let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it”, that is not for the man who isn't seeking counsel, who is watching porn, whatever he's doing, and then making decisions. You're going to make a mistake. In a multitude of counsel there is safety; the counsel of your own heart stands when it's funneled through the laws of God. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower”: the seven watchmen are godly men, and your own godly mind can see what's best for you.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a godly man, you go to God, and he directs your path. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners: “If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.” Your prayer for direction is only heard if your heart is not holding on to iniquity.

“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So it's not telling you not to get counsel from brothers. Get counsel, balance it with what you think might be right, with a godly mind, and then go to God and ask him to direct your path.

thread.label: Sirach 37:13
thread.text: And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.

classes.title: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.label: Proverbs 11:14
precepts.why:
Sirach says, “And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” But the scripture also says, “Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” At first that seems to be the total opposite. Should we not seek counsel?

In the multitude of counsellors there is safety means that as much counsel as you can get will help you make the right decisions and move in the right direction. That is correct. And the counsel of your own heart can stand only when it is funnelled through the laws of God, through the scriptures. Then you can make your decision and stand on it, because it is based on the laws of God.

Go up to verse 12 and it opens: “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should be spent around godly people, and if you lack understanding, around people with more understanding than you, so you can level up. You know who keeps the commandments by being exercised to discern between good and evil, and every beast consorts with its own kind. Such a man “will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he will correct you.

So letting the counsel of your own heart stand is not for the man who seeks no counsel and makes his decisions while watching porn. He is going to make a mistake. It is for the man whose mind is godly, like the godly man he took counsel from. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.”

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above your own heart and above the counsel of a friend, you go to God, and God does not hear the prayer of sinners. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So the two scriptures agree: get counsel from the brothers, balance it with what you think is right with a godly mind, then ask God to direct your path.

precepts.label: Ephesians 4:13
precepts.why:
Sirach describes the man who grows: “If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.” If you die, you leave a greater name than a thousand men, and if you live, your name keeps growing. That is a man who is ever evolving, always getting better, until we measure up unto the full stature of Christ. That measure is the goal the whole passage is climbing toward.

It comes in steps. First he serves “among great men” and appears “before princes”: studying four chapters a day, occupied in meditation and prophecies, keeping the sayings of the renowned men. Then he repents: he will “pray before the most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.” Then, “When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding”: when the Lord has seen you making a conscious change, mortifying and disciplining yourself. Before that, the strong meat is not for you. You have to learn the simple things first: no whoremonger shall enter the kingdom of heaven, wear your fringes, remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy, know the twelve tribes.

“In his secrets shall he meditate.” That is the transition from milk to meat. “He shall shew forth that which he hath learned”: out of his mouth comes the wisdom gathered over years of studying, applying, and getting around renowned men. “His name shall live from generation to generation.” That is what you want in your name, still part of the conversation after you leave this earth, for the wisdom God moved in you.

So you have to level up. As a teacher you cannot keep regurgitating the same classes over and over; you have to grow in understanding and application to teach the people. Growing to the full stature of Christ is how a name increases while you live.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:3-13
precepts.why:
Sirach says of David, “In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” But didn't David sin against God? He did. Yet “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” David sinned, but David repented, and God took away his sins.

This is how he repented: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” He confessed.

“Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” And after he confessed, what did David do? “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Get myself right, and then I'm going to go teach the people.

He teaches them “That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” Look at my example: it is good to follow the Lord, because in the end the Lord chose me as his friend.

David is a famous man, and he is an example for all of us. Some of us err in this truth, but you can recover yourself and still earn a name. You just have to do the work and be sincere. Much is given and much is required of us as leaders, so we have to be honest, confess, get clean, and then lead the people back to God.

thread.text: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.

classes.title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.label: Baruch 4:1-4
precepts.why:
Sirach ends the praise of Elias and Eliseus with the people after them: “Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.” So what is pleasing to God? Baruch answers it: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.”

Then: “O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.” The things pleasing to God are his laws. Us keeping the law is what pleases God. So when Sirach says some did that which was pleasing to God, it means some did the laws of God, and the rest multiplied sins.

That ties back to verse 10, where Elias was “ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” That is our job, before it breaks forth, before the decree brings forth and the fierce anger of God comes, as Zephaniah 3 says: to turn our people back to God.

What is well pleasing to God is for us to keep his laws first, and then become the prophets that lead the people back to them. Much is given, much is required of us in our walk as leaders.

precepts.label: Sirach 50:1
precepts.why:
After Josias, the twelve prophets, Zorobabel, Neemias and Joseph, Sirach carries the line of renowned men on to the priesthood: “Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple”. Simon repaired the house again. Like Neemias, “who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again”, his name is tied to building back what was broken down.

That is how these renowned men earned their names. It was about building back, walking in integrity, moving right. Josias “behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people”, not using his position to take advantage of the people or handling the word of God deceitfully. Neemias raised the walls and established the laws again, so nobody would come in trying to get our people to shop on the Sabbath. Simon repaired and fortified the house of God.

So it is with us: “in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of God.” In the midst of all this debauchery we are to establish the worship of God, with no hypocrisy, no covetousness and no murmuring, so that the people see us and say these are those guys we heard about that are going to come back on the earth. That is how you become the famous man.

The class only jumped through these chapters for time’s sake. Go through Sirach 44 to 50 again on your own, because there is a lot more in them.

thread.label: Baruch 4:1
thread.text: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.

classes.title: Ignite Your Influence

precepts.label: Proverbs 21:16
precepts.why:
Baruch says the law “endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” Since the beginning of time this law has been in place. Break it and judgments come upon you; keep it and blessings come upon you. Solomon shows what happens to those who leave it: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

Look at your old pictures and old videos from when you were in the world. You look dead, spiritually dead. Run down and tired, twenty-one years old looking forty, when that was supposed to be the pinnacle of life, of your youth. We wandered out of the way of understanding, and we were like the walking dead. That is why the law is called a spirit: the commandments are spirit, and without them there is no life in us.

They make those movies mocking us. We were the congregation of the dead. And it is ironic that zombies walk groping. That is groping at noonday, what the Lord said would come on us for breaking his commandments: walking around trying to catch on to something, gravitate to something, all confused in the spirit. Even with the sun at its apex we could not see. We were blinded. We were distracted.

So the law is the difference between the living and the dead. Those who keep it come to life, the way we did when we came into this truth; those who wander from it remain in the congregation of the dead.
